options.zh: 显出你考虑过另一面，然后才提出限制
options.en: shows that you have considered another side, and only then offered a limit

questions.stem_en: Name one common persuasive technique.
questions.explanation_en: Techniques should serve reasons.
questions.answer_zh: 如对照、修辞问句、让步后转折、具体例子。
questions.answer_en: For example: contrast, a rhetorical question, a concession then a turn, a concrete example.

questions.stem_zh: “Every careful student already agrees with me”的问题是？

is only informing the reader of tide times

questions.stem_zh: 评价一段劝说时，你应追问？

questions.explanation_zh: 理由是什么，是否忽略另一面。

options.zh: 能否把所有不同意见称为愚蠢

options.en: what the reason is, whether another side is ignored, and whether the tone threatens or flatters

questions.stem_zh: 具体的校园情境往往比“所有人都……”更站得住，因为？
questions.stem_en: A concrete school situation often stands more firmly than “everyone…” because it:
questions.explanation_en: Can be discussed and tested.

options.zh: 可以被讨论和检验，而不那么容易以偏概全

cannot be used in an argument

questions.answer_en: For example: Do you want an accident?

questions.stem_zh: 说服手法本身？
questions.stem_en: A persuasive technique itself is:
questions.explanation_zh: 不一定错误；错误在于代替证据或误导。

options.zh: 不一定错误；错误在于用它代替证据，或故意误导
options.en: not necessarily an error; the error is using it in place of evidence, or misleading on purpose

options.zh: 不能出现在课堂发言里

questions.stem_zh: 该发言更准确的立场是？
questions.stem_en: The more accurate stance of the extract is:
questions.explanation_zh: 并不相信“手机一定让我们更安全”。
questions.explanation_en: Not convinced that phones necessarily make us safer.

options.zh: 手机毫无用处，应全部禁止
options.en: phones are useless and should all be banned

options.zh: 并不相信“人人带手机就一定更安全”这一说法
options.en: not convinced by the claim that a phone in every pocket necessarily makes us safer
this is only a tide notice

questions.stem_zh: 评价立场时，首先应？
questions.stem_en: When evaluating a stance you should first:
questions.explanation_en: Restate it accurately in your own words.

options.zh: 用自己的话准确复述立场
options.en: restate the stance accurately in your own words

options.zh: 先把它改成极端观点再攻击
options.en: first turn it into an extreme view, then attack that

questions.stem_zh: 用一句话公正复述该发言的立场。

questions.answer: 说话人并不认为手机一定让人更安全
questions.explanation_en: Do not exaggerate it into “hates technology”.
accepted: 说话人并不认为手机一定让人更安全
他承认电话有用但也可能让人分心
The speaker is not convinced that phones necessarily make us safer
Phones can help but can also distract
questions.answer_zh: 说话人并不认为“人人带手机就一定更安全”。
questions.answer_en: The speaker is not convinced that phones necessarily make us safer.

questions.stem_zh: 该发言一个有效之处是？

questions.explanation_en: Admits a benefit of phones.

questions.stem_zh: 一个可能的不足是？
questions.stem_en: A possible limit is that it:

options.en: has too many reasons to be readable
should not have admitted any benefit

options.zh: 还缺少更具体的情境或证据，也尚未回应某些反驳
options.en: still lacks a more concrete situation or evidence, and has not yet met some replies

questions.stem_zh: 你的评价本身也需要？
questions.stem_en: Your evaluation itself also needs:
questions.explanation_en: Reasons.

options.zh: 理由，而不能只写喜欢或不喜欢
options.en: reasons, not only “I like it” or “I don’t”
an attack unrelated to the text

questions.stem_zh: 写出一个评价时可使用的四步顺序中的前两步。

a method for poetry appreciation only

questions.stem_zh: 短报告较完整的内容应包括？

Convert to consistent units, then use $v=s/t$
Speed does not depend on units

questions.stem_zh: 把 $10\ \text{m/s}$ 换算成 $\text{km/h}$。
questions.stem_en: Convert $10\ \text{m/s}$ into $\text{km/h}$.
questions.explanation_en: Multiply by $3.6$: $10\times 3.6=36\ \text{km/h}$.

questions.stem_zh: 写出计算速度的公式（可用符号 $v,s,t$ 或文字）。
questions.stem_en: Write the formula for speed (symbols $v,s,t$ or words).
questions.explanation_zh: 速度 = 路程 / 时间，即 $v=s/t$。
questions.explanation_en: Speed = distance / time, or $v=s/t$.

questions.stem_zh: 一名学生跑完 $200\ \text{m}$ 用了 $40\ \text{s}$。平均速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: A student runs $200\ \text{m}$ in $40\ \text{s}$. What is the average speed in $\text{m/s}$?

questions.stem_zh: 第 8 阶段公式 $v=s/t$ 中的 $s$ 通常表示？
questions.stem_en: In the Stage 8 formula $v=s/t$, $s$ usually stands for:
questions.explanation_zh: 这里 $s$ 表示路程（走过的距离）。位移需要考虑方向，本阶段课图与计算通常用路程。
questions.explanation_en: Here $s$ is distance (the length travelled). Displacement includes direction; Stage 8 calculations usually use distance.

options.zh: 只表示位移，不考虑路程

questions.stem_zh: 在路程—时间图像上，一段水平直线表示什么？
questions.stem_en: On a distance–time graph, what does a horizontal straight section show?
questions.explanation_zh: 路程不随时间增加，物体静止，速度为零。
questions.explanation_en: Distance is not increasing, so the object is stationary and the speed is zero.

questions.stem_zh: 路程—时间图像上直线更陡，通常表示？
questions.stem_en: A steeper straight line on a distance–time graph usually means:
questions.explanation_zh: 斜率（坡度）等于速度，更陡表示在相同时间内路程增加得更多，即速度更大。
questions.explanation_en: The gradient equals speed; a steeper line means more distance in the same time, so a greater speed.

options.en: the object must be slowing down

questions.stem_zh: 某图像在 $4\ \text{s}$ 内路程从 $0$ 均匀增加到 $20\ \text{m}$。这段的速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: On a graph, distance increases steadily from $0$ to $20\ \text{m}$ in $4\ \text{s}$. What is the speed in this interval, in $\text{m/s}$?
questions.explanation_en: Gradient $=\Delta s/\Delta t=20/4=5\ \text{m/s}$.

questions.stem_zh: 路程—时间图像的斜率（坡度）表示什么？
questions.stem_en: The gradient (slope) of a distance–time graph represents:
questions.explanation_zh: 斜率是路程的变化除以时间的变化，也就是速度。加速度要看速度—时间图像的斜率。
questions.explanation_en: Gradient is change in distance divided by change in time, which is speed. Acceleration is the gradient of a speed–time graph.

questions.stem_zh: 若图像先是向上的斜线，接着是一段水平线，物体后来在做什么？
questions.stem_en: A graph shows an upward straight line and then a horizontal section. What is the object doing in the later part?
questions.explanation_zh: 水平段表示路程不再增加，物体静止（停下）。
questions.explanation_en: The horizontal part means distance is no longer increasing: the object is stationary (it has stopped).

questions.stem_zh: 从 $t=0$ 到 $t=3\ \text{s}$，路程从 $2\ \text{m}$ 均匀增到 $14\ \text{m}$。速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: From $t=0$ to $t=3\ \text{s}$, distance rises steadily from $2\ \text{m}$ to $14\ \text{m}$. What is the speed in $\text{m/s}$?
questions.explanation_en: $\Delta s=14-2=12\ \text{m}$, $\Delta t=3\ \text{s}$, so speed $=12/3=4\ \text{m/s}$. Do not use $14/3$.

questions.stem_zh: 一段笔直向上的斜线（斜率不变）表示物体在这段时间内？
questions.stem_en: A straight upward line (constant gradient) means that, in that interval, the object:
questions.explanation_zh: 斜率不变就是速度恒定。曲线的斜率变化才表示速度在变。本阶段先掌握简单直线图像。
questions.explanation_en: A constant gradient means constant speed. A changing gradient (a curve) would mean a changing speed. Stage 8 starts with simple straight-line graphs.

options.en: has acceleration equal to the gradient

questions.stem_zh: 作用在物体上的力平衡（合力为零）时，物体将会？
questions.stem_en: When the forces on an object are balanced (resultant zero), the object will:
questions.explanation_zh: 平衡力使物体保持静止，或保持匀速直线运动，而不是一定停下，也不是开始加速。
questions.explanation_en: Balanced forces keep an object at rest, or moving at a constant speed in a straight line — not necessarily stopped, and not starting to accelerate.

options.zh: 保持静止或匀速直线运动
options.en: stay at rest or keep a steady speed in a straight line

questions.stem_zh: 非平衡力对运动的影响是？
questions.stem_en: An unbalanced force affects motion by:
questions.explanation_zh: 非平衡力会改变速度：加速、减速或改变方向。
questions.explanation_en: An unbalanced force changes velocity: it can speed an object up, slow it down or change its direction.

options.zh: 使物体加速、减速或改变方向
options.en: speeding it up, slowing it down or changing its direction

options.zh: 只能让静止的物体永远静止
options.en: only keeping a stationary object at rest forever
having no effect on motion at all

questions.stem_zh: 向右 $12\ \text{N}$、向左 $5\ \text{N}$，合力大小是多少牛顿？（只写数字）
questions.stem_en: Forces of $12\ \text{N}$ right and $5\ \text{N}$ left act on an object. What is the size of the resultant, in newtons? (number only)
questions.explanation_zh: 同一直线上，合力为较大的力减去较小的力：$12-5=7\ \text{N}$，方向向右。
questions.explanation_en: On a straight line, the resultant is the larger force minus the smaller: $12-5=7\ \text{N}$, to the right.

questions.stem_zh: 一本书静放在桌上。对书而言，下列说法正确的是？
questions.stem_en: A book rests on a table. Which statement is correct about the book?
questions.explanation_zh: 静止说明合力为零：重力与桌子的支持力平衡。不是“没有力”。
questions.explanation_en: Being at rest means the resultant is zero: weight is balanced by the support from the table. It is not “force-free”.

options.en: No forces act on the book

options.zh: 只有重力，所以它其实在加速
options.en: Only weight acts, so the book is really accelerating

options.zh: 合力向下，所以很快会掉下去
options.en: The resultant is downward, so it will soon fall

options.zh: 重力与支持力平衡，合力为零
options.en: Weight and the support force are balanced, so the resultant is zero

questions.stem_zh: 一个物体沿直线做匀速运动。作用在它上面的力是平衡的还是非平衡的？
questions.stem_en: An object moves in a straight line at constant speed. Are the forces on it balanced or unbalanced?
questions.explanation_zh: 匀速直线运动与静止一样，都是合力为零，力是平衡的。
questions.explanation_en: Steady motion in a straight line, like being at rest, means the resultant is zero: the forces are balanced.

questions.stem_zh: 足球在草地上越滚越慢，最合理的解释是？
questions.stem_en: A football rolling on grass slows down. The most reasonable explanation is:
questions.explanation_zh: 摩擦力等阻力是非平衡力，使球减速。不是因为“运动需要力来维持”所以力消失了。
questions.explanation_en: Friction and other resistances are unbalanced forces that slow the ball. It is not that “motion needs a force to keep going” and the force has vanished.

options.zh: 运动必须靠力维持，力用完了
options.en: Motion needs a force to keep going, and that force has run out

options.zh: 阻力与运动方向相反，合力不为零
options.en: Resistive forces opposite the motion give a non-zero resultant

questions.stem_zh: 向右推一只原来静止的箱子，且推力大于摩擦。箱子将会？
questions.stem_en: You push a previously resting box to the right, with a push larger than friction. The box will:
questions.explanation_zh: 原来静止，现在出现向右的合力，它会向右加速，而不是立刻获得恒定速度后永远不变。
questions.explanation_en: It was at rest; now there is a resultant to the right, so it speeds up to the right — it does not instantly take a speed that never changes.

options.zh: 仍然静止，因为曾经静止
options.en: stay at rest, because it was at rest

options.zh: 立刻以恒定速度向右，且无法再改变
options.en: instantly move right at a speed that can never change

questions.stem_zh: 一个大小为 $12\ \text{N}$ 的力，垂直力臂为 $0.5\ \text{m}$。力矩是多少 $\text{N\,m}$？
questions.stem_en: A force of $12\ \text{N}$ has a perpendicular distance of $0.5\ \text{m}$ from the pivot. What is the moment in $\text{N\,m}$?
questions.explanation_en: Moment $M=F\times d=12\times 0.5=6\ \text{N\,m}$.

questions.stem_zh: 计算力矩时，公式中的距离必须是？
questions.stem_en: In the moment formula, the distance must be:
questions.explanation_zh: 力臂是从支点到力的作用线的**垂直**距离，不是沿杆随便量的斜线长。
questions.explanation_en: The distance is the **perpendicular** distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force, not just any length along the bar.

options.en: any length measured along the bar

options.zh: 从支点到力的作用线的垂直距离
options.en: the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force

questions.stem_zh: 要用 $4\ \text{N}$ 的力产生 $10\ \text{N\,m}$ 的力矩，垂直力臂应为多少米？
questions.stem_en: What perpendicular distance, in metres, is needed for a $4\ \text{N}$ force to give a moment of $10\ \text{N\,m}$?

questions.stem_zh: 轻质杠杆平衡时，下列哪一项成立？
questions.stem_en: For a light lever in equilibrium, which statement is true?
questions.explanation_zh: 平衡时，顺时针力矩之和等于逆时针力矩之和。
questions.explanation_en: In equilibrium, the total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment.

options.zh: 顺时针力矩之和等于逆时针力矩之和
options.en: The total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment

options.zh: 两边的力必须相等，与距离无关
options.en: The two forces must be equal, whatever the distances

options.zh: 力矩必须为零且力也必须为零
options.en: Moments must be zero and all forces must be zero
A force on one side only is enough

questions.stem_zh: 支点左边 $20\ \text{N}$ 的力距支点 $0.4\ \text{m}$。右边用 $10\ \text{N}$ 平衡，它应距支点多少米？
questions.stem_en: On the left of a pivot, a $20\ \text{N}$ force acts $0.4\ \text{m}$ away. A $10\ \text{N}$ force on the right keeps balance. How far from the pivot, in metres, should it act?
questions.explanation_zh: 顺时针与逆时针力矩相等：$20\times 0.4=10\times d$，所以 $d=0.8\ \text{m}$。
questions.explanation_en: Clockwise and anticlockwise moments are equal: $20\times 0.4=10\times d$, so $d=0.8\ \text{m}$.

questions.stem_zh: 写出力矩的公式（可用 $M,F,d$ 或文字）。
questions.stem_en: Write the formula for a moment (symbols $M,F,d$ or words).
questions.explanation_zh: $M=F\times d$，其中 $d$ 是垂直力臂。文字：力矩 = 力 × 垂直距离。
questions.explanation_en: $M=F\times d$, where $d$ is the perpendicular distance. In words: moment = force × perpendicular distance.

questions.stem_zh: 同样大小的力，离支点越远，转向效果通常？
questions.stem_en: For the same size of force, a greater distance from the pivot usually makes the turning effect:
questions.explanation_zh: 力矩随垂直力臂增大而增大，所以同样的力离支点越远，越容易转动。
questions.explanation_en: Moment increases with perpendicular distance, so the same force turns more effectively farther from the pivot.

questions.stem_zh: 一个 $20\ \text{N}$ 的力作用在 $4\ \text{m}^2$ 的面积上。压强是多少 $\text{N/m}^2$？
questions.stem_en: A force of $20\ \text{N}$ acts on an area of $4\ \text{m}^2$. What is the pressure in $\text{N/m}^2$?
questions.explanation_en: Pressure $p=F/A=20/4=5\ \text{N/m}^2$.

questions.stem_zh: 在大小相同的力作用下，受力面积越小，压强？
questions.stem_en: For the same size of force, a smaller area means that pressure is:
questions.explanation_zh: $p=F/A$，面积越小压强越大。刀刃、图钉尖就是这个道理。
questions.explanation_en: $p=F/A$, so a smaller area gives a larger pressure. A knife edge or a drawing-pin tip works this way.

questions.stem_zh: 要用 $80\ \text{N}$ 的力在 $0.4\ \text{m}^2$ 上产生压强。压强是多少 $\text{N/m}^2$？
questions.stem_en: An $80\ \text{N}$ force acts on $0.4\ \text{m}^2$. What is the pressure in $\text{N/m}^2$?

questions.stem_zh: 写出压强的公式（可用 $p,F,A$ 或文字）。
questions.stem_en: Write the formula for pressure (symbols $p,F,A$ or words).
questions.explanation_en: $p=F/A$, that is pressure = force / area.

questions.stem_zh: 雪地靴比普通鞋更不容易陷进雪里，主要是因为？
questions.stem_en: Snowshoes are less likely than ordinary shoes to sink into snow mainly because they:
questions.explanation_zh: 面积更大，同一个人的重力被分摊，压强减小。不是人变轻了。
questions.explanation_en: They have a larger area, so the same weight is spread out and pressure falls. The person is not lighter.

options.en: reduce the mass of the snow

options.zh: 增大接触面积，从而减小压强
options.en: increase the contact area and so reduce the pressure

questions.stem_zh: 压强为 $25\ \text{N/m}^2$，面积为 $2\ \text{m}^2$。力是多少牛顿？
questions.stem_en: The pressure is $25\ \text{N/m}^2$ on an area of $2\ \text{m}^2$. What is the force in newtons?
questions.explanation_en: $F=pA=25\times 2=50\ \text{N}$.

questions.stem_zh: 压强的单位 $\text{N/m}^2$ 与力矩的单位 $\text{N\,m}$ 容易混淆。压强是？
questions.stem_en: The pressure unit $\text{N/m}^2$ is easy to confuse with the moment unit $\text{N\,m}$. Pressure is:
questions.explanation_zh: 压强是力除以面积（$\text{N/m}^2$ 或帕斯卡）；力矩是力乘以距离（$\text{N\,m}$）。
questions.explanation_en: Pressure is force divided by area ($\text{N/m}^2$ or pascal); a moment is force times distance ($\text{N\,m}$).

questions.stem_zh: 气体对器壁产生压强，主要是因为粒子？
questions.stem_en: A gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container mainly because the particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 气体粒子不断运动并碰撞器壁，每次碰撞都给器壁一个力，大量碰撞形成压强。
questions.explanation_en: Gas particles move continually and collide with the walls; each collision exerts a force, and many collisions produce pressure.

options.en: all sit still at the bottom
move continually and collide with the walls

options.zh: 彼此吸引并把容器拉小
options.en: attract each other and shrink the container

options.zh: 没有质量所以能穿过器壁
options.en: have no mass and pass through the walls

questions.stem_zh: 温度升高时（体积大致不变），气体压强通常会？
questions.stem_en: If the temperature rises (and the volume stays about the same), the pressure of a gas usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 粒子运动更快，碰撞更频繁也更有力，压强增大。
questions.explanation_en: Particles move faster, so collisions are more frequent and harder, and the pressure rises.

options.zh: 增大，因为碰撞更频繁、更有力
options.en: increase, because collisions are more frequent and harder

options.zh: 减小，因为粒子停止运动
options.en: decrease, because the particles stop moving

questions.stem_zh: 同一温度下，把气体压缩到更小体积，压强通常？
questions.stem_en: At the same temperature, compressing a gas into a smaller volume usually makes the pressure:
questions.explanation_zh: 同样多的粒子在更小空间里，单位时间碰撞器壁更频繁，压强增大。
questions.explanation_en: The same number of particles in a smaller space hit the walls more often, so the pressure rises.

options.en: depend only on the colour of the container

questions.stem_zh: 用粒子的观点，一句话解释气体为什么有压强。
questions.stem_en: In one sentence, explain gas pressure in terms of particles.
questions.explanation_zh: 气体粒子不断碰撞器壁，大量碰撞产生一个平均的力，从而形成压强。
questions.explanation_en: Gas particles continually collide with the walls; many collisions produce an average force and therefore a pressure.

questions.stem_zh: 液体内部也有压强。与气体相比，液体粒子？
questions.stem_en: Liquids also exert pressure. Compared with a gas, liquid particles are:
questions.explanation_zh: 液体粒子更紧密，几乎不可压缩，但仍然运动并相互碰撞，也对接触面施力。
questions.explanation_en: Liquid particles are much closer together and almost incompressible, but they still move and collide, and they exert forces on surfaces they touch.

options.en: spaced exactly as in a gas

options.zh: 可以自由飞过很大的空间
options.en: free to fly across large empty spaces

options.zh: 靠得更近，几乎不可压缩，仍会碰撞并施力
options.en: closer together, almost incompressible, and still collide and exert forces

questions.stem_zh: 给轮胎打气时压强升高，一个合理的粒子解释是？
questions.stem_en: When you pump more air into a tyre, the pressure rises. A reasonable particle explanation is:
questions.explanation_zh: 更多粒子在相近体积里，单位时间碰撞内壁更频繁，压强增大。
questions.explanation_en: More particles in a similar volume hit the inner wall more often, so the pressure rises.

options.zh: 更多粒子更频繁地碰撞内壁
options.en: more particles collide with the inner wall more often
air is no longer made of particles

questions.stem_zh: 下列哪一项最能说明“压强来自粒子碰撞”，而不是“空气有重量所以向下压”这一种不完整的说法？
questions.stem_en: Which observation best supports “pressure comes from particle collisions”, rather than the incomplete idea that “air only pushes down because it has weight”?
questions.explanation_zh: 封闭容器中气体对各个方向的器壁（包括向上、向侧面）都有压强，说明是各向碰撞，不只是“向下的重量”。
questions.explanation_en: A gas in a closed container pushes on every wall — including upwards and sideways — which fits collisions in all directions, not only a downward weight.

options.en: A gas only pushes on the bottom of a container
Pressure is greatest in a vacuum

options.zh: 气体对上、下、侧面的器壁都有压强
options.en: A gas exerts pressure on the top, bottom and sides of a container

questions.stem_zh: 扩散能够发生，是因为粒子？
questions.stem_en: Diffusion can happen because particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 粒子在不断随机运动，因而会从浓度高的区域逐渐散布到浓度低的区域。
questions.explanation_en: Particles move continually and randomly, so they gradually spread from where they are more concentrated to where they are less concentrated.

options.en: can only move if an outside force pushes them

options.zh: 在液体中完全不能运动
options.en: cannot move at all in a liquid

questions.stem_zh: 一般来说，气体中的扩散比液体中更快，主要是因为气体粒子？
questions.stem_en: Diffusion is generally faster in a gas than in a liquid mainly because gas particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 气体粒子间距更大、运动更自由，彼此阻碍较少，所以扩散通常更快。液体粒子更紧密。
questions.explanation_en: Gas particles are more widely spaced and move more freely, with fewer collisions that hinder spreading, so diffusion is usually faster. Liquid particles are much closer.

options.en: are more widely spaced and move more freely

options.zh: 质量一定比液体粒子大得多
options.en: must have a much larger mass than liquid particles
must be at a much lower temperature

questions.stem_zh: 温度升高时，扩散通常会？
questions.stem_en: If the temperature rises, diffusion usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 粒子平均运动更快，因而扩散加快。
questions.explanation_en: Particles move faster on average, so diffusion speeds up.

options.zh: 加快，因为粒子运动更快
options.en: speed up, because the particles move faster

questions.stem_zh: 用粒子的观点，简要解释香水味为什么能在房间里传播。
questions.stem_en: In terms of particles, briefly explain why the smell of perfume can spread across a room.
questions.explanation_zh: 香水的粒子不断运动，并在空气粒子之间扩散，从浓度高的地方逐渐散布到整个房间。
questions.explanation_en: Perfume particles move continually and diffuse among the air particles, spreading from a region of higher concentration across the room.

questions.stem_zh: 在装满水的烧杯中滴入一滴色素，色素会慢慢散开。这主要是？
questions.stem_en: A drop of dye in a beaker of water slowly spreads out. This is mainly:
questions.explanation_zh: 这是液体中的扩散：色素粒子与水粒子都在运动并逐渐混合。不是整杯水被搅拌，也不是重力把颜色“拉”匀。
questions.explanation_en: This is diffusion in a liquid: dye particles and water particles move and gradually mix. The water need not be stirred, and gravity does not “pull the colour even”.

options.en: something that can only happen if the water is stirred hard
the dye turning into a gas

options.zh: 杯底出现了一个力把颜色拉下去
options.en: a force at the bottom pulling the colour down

questions.stem_zh: 下列哪一项最准确地描述扩散的方向？
questions.stem_en: Which statement describes the overall direction of diffusion most accurately?
questions.explanation_zh: 总体上看，粒子从浓度较高的区域净迁移到浓度较低的区域，直到比较均匀。个别粒子路径是随机的。
questions.explanation_en: Overall, there is a net movement from higher to lower concentration until the mixture is more uniform. Individual particle paths are random.

options.zh: 总体上从浓度高处到浓度低处
options.en: overall, from higher to lower concentration

options.zh: 只能从低浓度到高浓度
options.en: only from lower to higher concentration

options.zh: 粒子沿一条直线同时到达各处
options.en: particles travel in a straight line and arrive everywhere at once
it happens only in a vacuum

questions.stem_zh: 两瓶气体之间用细管相连后，较轻的气体往往扩散得更快。一个合理的解释是？
questions.stem_en: Two gases are linked by a narrow tube. The lighter gas often diffuses faster. A reasonable explanation is that lighter particles typically:
questions.explanation_zh: 在相近温度下，较轻的粒子平均速率往往更大，因而扩散更快。这是一个简化的第 8 阶段解释。
questions.explanation_en: At a similar temperature, lighter particles typically have a greater average speed, so they diffuse faster. This is a simplified Stage 8 explanation.

options.en: can move only in a liquid

questions.stem_zh: 反射定律指出，入射角与反射角？
questions.stem_en: The law of reflection says that the angle of incidence and the angle of reflection are:
questions.explanation_zh: 二者相等，且入射光线、法线、反射光线在同一平面内。
questions.explanation_en: They are equal, and the incident ray, the normal and the reflected ray lie in the same plane.

options.zh: 与表面材质无关且可以任意取值
options.en: independent of the surface and can take any values

questions.stem_zh: 入射角和反射角是从哪一条线量起的？
questions.stem_en: The angles of incidence and reflection are measured from:
questions.explanation_zh: 必须从法线（与镜面垂直的虚线）量起，不是从镜面量起。
questions.explanation_en: They are measured from the normal (the dashed line at right angles to the mirror), not from the surface of the mirror.

options.zh: 入射光线到反射光线之间
options.en: the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray
the normal (the line at right angles to the surface)
the line from the lamp to the eye

questions.stem_zh: 光线射到平面镜，入射角为 $35^\circ$。反射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: A ray strikes a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of $35^\circ$. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation_zh: 反射定律：$i=r$，所以反射角也是 $35^\circ$。
questions.explanation_en: The law of reflection: $i=r$, so the angle of reflection is also $35^\circ$.

questions.stem_zh: 若入射光线与镜面的夹角为 $30^\circ$，入射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: A ray makes a $30^\circ$ angle with the mirror surface. What is the angle of incidence, in degrees?
questions.explanation_zh: 法线与镜面垂直，所以入射角 $=90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$，不是 $30^\circ$。
questions.explanation_en: The normal is at $90^\circ$ to the mirror, so the angle of incidence is $90^\circ-30^\circ=60^\circ$, not $30^\circ$.

questions.stem_zh: 用一句话写出平面镜的反射定律。
questions.stem_en: State the law of reflection at a plane surface in one sentence.
questions.explanation_zh: 入射角等于反射角（从法线量起），且入射光线、法线、反射光线在同一平面内。
questions.explanation_en: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (measured from the normal), and the incident ray, normal and reflected ray lie in the same plane.
accepted: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection

questions.stem_zh: 画平面镜光线图时，法线应该？
questions.stem_en: When you draw a ray diagram for a plane mirror, the normal should be:
questions.explanation_zh: 在入射点与镜面垂直，通常画成虚线，作为量角的基准。
questions.explanation_en: Drawn at right angles to the mirror at the point of incidence, usually dashed, as the reference for measuring the angles.

options.zh: 过入射点并与镜面垂直，常画成虚线
options.en: at right angles to the mirror at the point of incidence, often dashed

options.zh: 可省略，因为角度从镜面量更方便
options.en: left out, because it is easier to measure from the mirror

questions.stem_zh: 平面镜反射可以用来？
questions.stem_en: Reflection at a plane surface can be used to:
questions.explanation_zh: 平面镜按定律改变光线方向，可用于观察拐角、改变光路等。第 8 阶段只要能陈述定律并画简单图。
questions.explanation_en: A plane mirror changes the direction of rays according to the law, for example to look around a corner or redirect a beam. Stage 8 asks you to state the law and draw a simple diagram.

options.zh: 把白光分解成光谱（这是色散）
options.en: split white light into a spectrum (that is dispersion)

options.zh: 让光线在玻璃中永远拐弯（这是折射）
options.en: make light bend forever inside glass (that is refraction)

options.zh: 按 $i=r$ 改变光线方向，如用镜子观察或反射光束
options.en: change a ray’s direction with $i=r$, for example with a mirror

questions.stem_zh: 光线从空气斜射入玻璃时，通常会？
questions.stem_en: When a ray travels from air into glass at an angle, it usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入玻璃（光密介质）时，光线向法线偏折，折射角小于入射角。
questions.explanation_en: Entering glass (an optically denser medium), the ray bends towards the normal, so the angle of refraction is smaller than the angle of incidence.

options.zh: 一定沿原方向，永不偏折
options.en: always continue in a straight line with no bending

options.zh: 被完全反射，再也不能进入玻璃
options.en: be totally reflected and never enter the glass

questions.stem_zh: 光线从玻璃斜射回空气时，通常会？
questions.stem_en: When a ray travels from glass into air at an angle, it usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入空气（光疏介质）时，光线远离法线，折射角大于入射角。
questions.explanation_en: Entering air (an optically less dense medium), the ray bends away from the normal, so the angle of refraction is larger than the angle of incidence.

options.en: keep the same speed and so not bend

options.zh: 颜色立刻变成单一红色
options.en: instantly become a single red colour

questions.stem_zh: 折射中的入射角和折射角同样是从哪一条线量起？
questions.stem_en: In refraction, the angles of incidence and refraction are also measured from:
questions.explanation_zh: 和反射一样，必须从法线量起。
questions.explanation_en: As with reflection, they are measured from the normal.

options.en: the extension of the ray itself

questions.stem_zh: 光线从空气垂直（沿法线）射入玻璃，方向会怎样？
questions.stem_en: A ray travels from air into glass along the normal (straight on). What happens to its direction?
questions.explanation_zh: 沿法线入射时不偏折，方向不变，但在玻璃中速度会变慢。
questions.explanation_en: Along the normal there is no bending: the direction stays the same, although the light slows down in the glass.

questions.stem_zh: 空气—水界面上的折射，与空气—玻璃相比？
questions.stem_en: Refraction at an air–water boundary, compared with air–glass:
questions.explanation_zh: 道理相同：进入水（比空气光密）时向法线偏折。偏折程度可以不同，但规则一样。
questions.explanation_en: The same rule applies: entering water (optically denser than air) the ray bends towards the normal. The amount of bending may differ, but the rule is the same.

options.en: light does not refract in water
it only works in sea water

options.zh: 同样是进入更光密介质时向法线偏折
options.en: again, the ray bends towards the normal when entering a denser medium

questions.stem_zh: 为什么池底看起来比实际更浅，一个光学原因是？
questions.stem_en: A pool can look shallower than it really is. One optical reason is:
questions.explanation_zh: 从水中射向空气的光线在水面远离法线偏折，我们沿直线追迹光线，会觉得池底被“抬高”了。
questions.explanation_en: Rays from the water bend away from the normal at the surface; we trace them back in straight lines and the bottom appears raised.

options.zh: 水中射出的光线在水面远离法线，看起来池底被抬高
options.en: rays leaving the water bend away from the normal, so the bottom looks raised
the water absorbs all the light
it is only to do with magnetism
the law of reflection has failed

questions.stem_zh: 第 8 阶段讨论的空气—玻璃或空气—水折射，正确的图应画出？
questions.stem_en: A correct Stage 8 diagram for air–glass or air–water refraction should show:
questions.explanation_zh: 界面、法线、入射光线和折射光线，并标出从法线量起的角。不要把折射画成反射那样 $i=r$。
questions.explanation_en: The boundary, the normal, the incident ray and the refracted ray, with angles marked from the normal. Do not draw refraction as if $i=r$.

options.zh: 只有反射光线，没有进入第二种介质的光线
options.en: only a reflected ray, with no ray entering the second medium

options.zh: 界面、法线、入射光线和折射光线
options.en: the boundary, the normal, the incident ray and the refracted ray

options.zh: 把玻璃画成一面普通平面镜即可
options.en: the glass drawn simply as an ordinary plane mirror

questions.stem_zh: 白光通过三棱镜后展开成光谱，这种现象称为？
questions.stem_en: White light spread into a spectrum by a triangular prism is called:
questions.explanation_zh: 这是色散：白光由不同颜色的光组成，它们在玻璃中偏折程度不同。
questions.explanation_en: This is dispersion: white light is made of different colours, which are bent by different amounts in glass.

questions.stem_zh: 在玻璃棱镜产生的光谱中，通常偏折最大的可见光是？
questions.stem_en: In the spectrum produced by a glass prism, the visible colour that is usually bent the most is:
questions.explanation_zh: 紫光通常偏折最大，红光偏折最小。顺序可记为红橙黄绿蓝靛紫。
questions.explanation_en: Violet is usually bent the most, and red the least. A useful order is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

questions.stem_zh: 白光色散说明白光？
questions.stem_en: The dispersion of white light shows that white light:
questions.explanation_zh: 白光不是单一颜色，而是由多种色光混合而成。
questions.explanation_en: White light is not a single colour; it is a mixture of different colours.

options.zh: 本身只有一种颜色，棱镜“制造”了其他颜色
options.en: is itself only one colour, and the prism “creates” the others
is made up of a range of colours
is the same kind of wave as sound

questions.stem_zh: 在可见光谱里，哪一种色光通过棱镜时通常偏折最小？
questions.stem_en: Which visible colour is usually bent the least by a prism?
questions.explanation_zh: 红光偏折最小，紫光偏折最大。
questions.explanation_en: Red is bent the least, and violet the most.

questions.stem_zh: 色散能够发生，是因为不同色光在玻璃中？
questions.stem_en: Dispersion happens because different colours in glass:
questions.explanation_zh: 不同色光折射率不同，因而折射角不同，离开棱镜后被分开。
questions.explanation_en: Different colours have slightly different refractive effects, so they leave the prism in slightly different directions and separate.

options.zh: 速度和方向都绝对相同
options.en: travel at exactly the same speed and in exactly the same direction

options.zh: 全部被镜面反射，角度相同
options.en: are all reflected from a mirror at the same angle

options.zh: 偏折程度略有不同，因而被分开
options.en: are bent by slightly different amounts and so separate

questions.stem_zh: 若把光谱中的各色光再适当会合，可能得到？
questions.stem_en: If the colours of the spectrum are recombined in a suitable way, you may obtain:
questions.explanation_zh: 各色光是从白光分开的，再会合可以重新得到白光。这说明棱镜并没有“制造”新的颜色。
questions.explanation_en: The colours were separated from white light, so recombining them can give white light again. The prism did not “create” new colours.

questions.stem_zh: 画棱镜色散图时，白光从一边射入，另一边应画出？
questions.stem_en: On a prism dispersion diagram, white light enters one side. The other side should show:
questions.explanation_zh: 展开的光谱，红光偏折较小、紫光偏折较大，中间是其他可见色光。
questions.explanation_en: A spread spectrum, with red bent less than violet, and the other visible colours in between.

options.zh: 一条不偏折的白光，完全不变
options.en: a single undeviated white ray, unchanged

options.zh: 只有反射回原路的光线
options.en: only a ray reflected back the way it came

options.zh: 分开的色光，红偏折较小、紫偏折较大
options.en: separated colours, red bent less than violet

options.zh: 与入射白光完全对称的一条黑线
options.en: a black line exactly symmetrical to the incoming white ray

questions.stem_zh: 红光与绿光按一定方式叠加，通常可以得到？
questions.stem_en: Red light and green light added in a suitable way usually give:
questions.explanation_zh: 红加绿可以得到黄。这是色光的叠加（加色）。
questions.explanation_en: Red plus green can give yellow. This is addition of coloured light (additive colour).

options.zh: 与颜料完全相同的结果，所以一定是蓝
options.en: exactly the same result as with paints, so it must be blue

questions.stem_zh: 红、绿、蓝三束色光适当叠加，可以得到？
questions.stem_en: Red, green and blue light added in a suitable way can give:
questions.explanation_zh: 这三种是常用的加色三原色，适当叠加可以得到白光。
questions.explanation_en: These are the usual additive primary colours; added suitably they can give white light.

questions.stem_zh: 白光照射一块只反射绿光、吸收其他可见光的物体，它看起来通常是？
questions.stem_en: White light falls on an object that reflects only green light and absorbs the other visible colours. The object usually looks:
questions.explanation_zh: 我们看到的是被反射进入眼睛的色光。只反射绿光的物体看起来是绿色的。
questions.explanation_en: We see the coloured light that is reflected into the eye. An object that reflects only green looks green.

options.zh: 白色，因为入射光是白光
options.en: white, because the incoming light is white

options.zh: 黑色，因为吸收了部分光
options.en: black, because some light is absorbed

options.zh: 没有颜色，因为光被吸收了就看不见物体
options.en: colourless, because absorbed light means the object cannot be seen

questions.stem_zh: 白光下看起来是红色的滤光片，主要作用通常是？
questions.stem_en: A filter that looks red in white light usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 滤光片透射某些色光、吸收另一些。红滤光片主要让红光通过，吸收大部分其他可见光。
questions.explanation_en: A filter transmits some colours and absorbs others. A red filter mainly lets red through and absorbs most other visible colours.

options.en: turns all the light into a magnetic field

options.zh: 主要透射红光，吸收其他许多色光
options.en: mainly transmits red light and absorbs many other colours

questions.stem_zh: 几乎吸收全部可见光、几乎不反射的物体，看起来是什么颜色？
questions.stem_en: What colour does an object look if it absorbs almost all visible light and reflects almost none?
questions.explanation_zh: 几乎没有色光进入眼睛，物体看起来是黑色的。
questions.explanation_en: Almost no coloured light reaches the eye, so the object looks black.

questions.stem_zh: 蓝光照射一块只能反射红光（吸收蓝光）的物体，它看起来最可能是？
questions.stem_en: Blue light falls on an object that can reflect only red light (and absorbs blue). The object is most likely to look:
questions.explanation_zh: 入射光中几乎没有可被反射的红光，蓝光又被吸收，进入眼睛的光很少，物体看起来很暗或接近黑色。
questions.explanation_en: There is almost no red light to reflect, and the blue is absorbed, so little light reaches the eye and the object looks very dark or nearly black.

options.zh: 明亮的红色，与白光下完全一样
options.en: bright red, exactly as in white light

questions.stem_zh: 色光的叠加与颜料的混合常常不同。一个关键差别是？
questions.stem_en: Adding coloured lights is often different from mixing paints. A key difference is that:
questions.explanation_zh: 色光叠加是把光加在一起（加色）；颜料更多地是吸收（减色）。红光加绿光可得黄，红颜料加绿颜料通常得不到明亮的黄光效果。
questions.explanation_en: Adding lights puts light together (additive); paints mainly absorb (subtractive). Red light plus green light can give yellow; red and green paints usually do not give a bright yellow-light effect.

options.zh: 二者在任何情况下结果都完全一样
options.en: the results are identical in every case

options.zh: 色光是叠加（加色），颜料更多是吸收（减色）
颜料会发光，色光只会吸收
options.en: paints emit light, and coloured light only absorbs

options.zh: 只有颜料遵守反射定律
options.en: only paints obey the law of reflection

questions.stem_zh: 绿光与品红光（品红可看作红加蓝）适当叠加，最可能得到？
questions.stem_en: Green light and magenta light (magenta can be thought of as red plus blue) added suitably are most likely to give:
questions.explanation_zh: 品红含红与蓝，再加绿，相当于红绿蓝会合，可得白光。这是色光叠加，不是颜料混合。
questions.explanation_en: Magenta contains red and blue; adding green is like bringing red, green and blue together, which can give white. This is addition of light, not mixing paint.

questions.stem_zh: 磁场最简明的含义是？
questions.stem_en: A magnetic field is, in brief:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁场是磁体周围有磁力作用的空间。
questions.explanation_en: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet where magnetic forces act.

options.zh: 只有真空中才有的声音
options.en: a sound that exists only in a vacuum

options.zh: 磁体周围有磁力作用的空间
options.en: the region around a magnet where magnetic forces act
just another name for electric current
a temperature field unrelated to magnets

questions.stem_zh: 画条形磁体的磁场方向时，磁感线在磁体外通常画成？
questions.stem_en: For the field around a bar magnet, field lines outside the magnet are usually drawn:
questions.explanation_zh: 在磁体外，磁感线从 N 极出发，回到 S 极。箭头表示放在该处的小磁针 N 极受力方向。
questions.explanation_en: Outside the magnet, field lines leave the N pole and return to the S pole. The arrows show the direction of the force on the N pole of a small compass needle.

options.zh: 从 N 极出发，回到 S 极
options.en: leaving the N pole and returning to the S pole

options.zh: 从 S 极出发，回到 N 极
options.en: leaving the S pole and returning to the N pole

options.zh: 只画封闭的正方形，没有方向
options.en: as closed squares with no direction

options.zh: 全部平行于地面且没有起点
options.en: all parallel to the ground with no starting point

questions.stem_zh: 磁感线画得更密的地方，通常表示磁场？
questions.stem_en: Where field lines are drawn closer together, the magnetic field is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁感线越密，磁场越强，例如靠近磁极处。
questions.explanation_en: Closer field lines mean a stronger field, for example near the poles.

options.en: unrelated to how close the lines are

questions.stem_zh: 用什么简单仪器可以显示磁体周围磁场的方向？
questions.stem_en: What simple instrument can show the direction of the field around a magnet?
questions.explanation_zh: 小磁针（指南针）的 N 极指向该处磁场的方向。也可用铁屑显示磁感线的形状。
questions.explanation_en: A plotting compass (the N pole of a small needle) points in the direction of the field. Iron filings can show the shape of the field.

questions.stem_zh: 两个磁极靠近时，下列说法正确的是？
questions.stem_en: When two magnetic poles are brought close together, which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 同名磁极相斥，异名磁极相吸。这是磁场对另一个磁极施加力的表现。
questions.explanation_en: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract. That is the field exerting a force on another pole.

options.en: There is never a force between poles

options.zh: 只有 S 极之间有力

options.en: Like poles repel and unlike poles attract

questions.stem_zh: 磁场是一种模型。磁感线是？
questions.stem_en: A magnetic field is a model. Field lines are:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁感线是帮助我们描述磁场方向和强弱的图示，并不是一根根真实的绳子。
questions.explanation_en: Field lines are a diagram to help us describe the direction and strength of the field; they are not real strings in space.

options.zh: 用来表示方向和相对强弱的图线，不是真实的绳子
options.en: diagram lines for direction and relative strength, not real strings
thin iron wires you can pick up

questions.stem_zh: 在条形磁体的中垂线上、离磁体较远处，与靠近磁极处相比，磁场通常？
questions.stem_en: On the perpendicular bisector of a bar magnet, far from the magnet, the field compared with a point near a pole is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 远离磁体处磁感线较疏，磁场较弱。
questions.explanation_en: Farther away the field lines are more spaced out, so the field is weaker.

options.en: impossible to test with a compass

options.zh: 一定完全消失且不可再检测

questions.stem_zh: 最简单的电磁铁通常是？
questions.stem_en: The simplest electromagnet is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 在铁芯上绕绝缘导线，通以电流，铁芯就被磁化，成为电磁铁。
questions.explanation_en: Insulated wire wound around an iron core, with a current in the coil, magnetises the core and makes an electromagnet.

options.zh: 一块永远不能关断的永磁体
options.en: a permanent magnet that can never be switched off

options.zh: 绕在铁芯上的线圈，并通以电流
options.en: a coil of wire around an iron core, with a current in the coil
a wooden rod not connected to a circuit

questions.stem_zh: 电磁铁相对于永磁体的一个重要优点是？
questions.stem_en: An important advantage of an electromagnet compared with a permanent magnet is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 切断电流后磁性可以大大减弱或消失，因此能够开关，便于控制和放工件。
questions.explanation_en: When the current is switched off the magnetism can fall greatly or vanish, so it can be switched, controlled, and used to drop a load.

options.zh: 可以通断电来开关磁性
options.en: can be switched on and off by switching the current

questions.stem_zh: 断开电源后，电磁铁通常会？
questions.stem_en: When the current is switched off, an electromagnet usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 线圈产生的磁场随之消失（铁芯可能留下很弱的剩磁），因此能放下被吸住的铁质物体。
questions.explanation_en: The field due to the coil disappears (the core may keep a weak remnant), so a lifted iron object can be released.

options.zh: 磁性大大减弱或消失，可放下工件
options.en: lose most or all of its magnetism, so a load can be dropped

options.zh: 变成更强的永磁体，再也放不下东西
options.en: become a stronger permanent magnet and never release a load

questions.stem_zh: 为什么电磁铁的线圈常用绝缘导线？
questions.stem_en: Why is the wire in an electromagnet coil usually insulated?
questions.explanation_zh: 绝缘避免相邻线圈直接短路，电流才能沿线圈一圈圈绕过铁芯。
questions.explanation_en: Insulation stops neighbouring turns shorting; the current can then travel around the core turn by turn.

questions.stem_zh: 电磁铁常用于？
questions.stem_en: Electromagnets are commonly used in:
questions.explanation_zh: 例如废铁场的起重电磁铁、电铃、继电器、某些门锁等，都需要可开关的磁性。
questions.explanation_en: Examples include scrap-yard lifting magnets, electric bells, relays and some door locks — all need magnetism that can be switched.

options.zh: 只能测量路程—时间图像的斜率
options.en: measuring the gradient of a distance–time graph only

options.zh: 可开关的起重、电铃、继电器等
options.en: switchable lifting, bells, relays and similar devices

questions.stem_zh: 铁芯的作用主要是？
questions.stem_en: The main job of the iron core is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 铁是磁性材料，能使线圈的磁场大大增强并集中。常用软铁，以便断电后磁性尽快减弱。
questions.explanation_en: Iron is a magnetic material, so it greatly strengthens and concentrates the field of the coil. Soft iron is used so that the magnetism falls quickly when the current stops.

options.en: turn the coil into an insulator
strengthen and concentrate the magnetic field

questions.stem_zh: 制作并使用电磁铁时，一个必要的条件是？
questions.stem_en: A necessary condition when making and using an electromagnet is:
questions.explanation_zh: 必须有电流通过线圈。没有电流，就没有这种可开关的磁场。
questions.explanation_en: There must be a current in the coil. Without a current there is no such switchable field.

options.en: the coil must be immersed in mercury

options.zh: 周围必须完全没有空气
options.en: there must be no air at all around it

questions.stem_zh: 在其他条件相近时，增大线圈中的电流，电磁铁通常会？
questions.stem_en: If other conditions are similar, increasing the current in the coil usually makes an electromagnet:
questions.explanation_zh: 电流越大，磁场通常越强，能吸起的回形针往往越多。
questions.explanation_en: A larger current usually means a stronger field, so the electromagnet can often lift more paper clips.

questions.stem_zh: 在其他条件相近时，增加线圈匝数，电磁铁通常会？
questions.stem_en: If other conditions are similar, increasing the number of turns on the coil usually makes an electromagnet:
questions.explanation_zh: 匝数越多，磁场通常越强。
questions.explanation_en: More turns usually mean a stronger field.

questions.stem_zh: 比较有铁芯与空心线圈（其他条件相近），通常？
questions.stem_en: Comparing a coil with an iron core and an air-cored coil (other conditions similar), usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 铁芯能显著增强磁场，有铁芯的电磁铁更强。
questions.explanation_en: An iron core greatly strengthens the field, so the electromagnet with a core is stronger.

options.en: the air-cored coil is always stronger
the one with an iron core is stronger
the core only weakens the field

questions.stem_zh: 列出两个能使电磁铁更强的因素。
questions.stem_en: Name two factors that can make an electromagnet stronger.
questions.explanation_zh: 例如：增大电流；增加匝数；加入（软）铁芯。答出其中两个即可。
questions.explanation_en: For example: a larger current; more turns; adding a (soft) iron core. Any two of these are enough.

questions.stem_zh: 做对比实验时，要比较匝数的影响，应？
questions.stem_en: In a fair test of the effect of the number of turns, you should:
questions.explanation_zh: 只改变匝数，尽量保持电流、铁芯、回形针种类等其他因素不变。
questions.explanation_en: Change only the number of turns, and keep current, core, type of clips and other factors as steady as possible.

options.zh: 同时随意改电流、铁芯和匝数
options.en: change current, core and turns all at once, at random

options.zh: 不必记录吸起的回形针数目
options.en: not bother recording how many clips are lifted

options.zh: 每次都换一种完全不同的测量方法且不说明
options.en: change the measuring method every time without comment

options.zh: 只改变匝数，控制其他变量
options.en: change only the number of turns and control the other variables

questions.stem_zh: 用吸起回形针的数目比较强弱时，若电流过大导致导线明显发热，可能的问题是？
questions.stem_en: If you compare strength by counting paper clips, but a very large current makes the wire heat up badly, a problem is:
questions.explanation_zh: 过热可能改变电阻甚至损坏绝缘，实验不再公平，也有安全风险。电流要在安全范围内增大。
questions.explanation_en: Overheating can change the resistance or damage the insulation, so the test is no longer fair, and it can be unsafe. Increase the current only within a safe range.

options.zh: 实验可能不再公平，且有安全风险
options.en: the test may no longer be fair, and it may be unsafe

options.zh: 发热证明电磁铁一定变弱了
options.en: heating proves the electromagnet must have become weaker

options.zh: 这时应立刻把铁芯换成塑料
options.en: you should immediately replace the core with plastic

questions.stem_zh: 在安全、其他条件相同的前提下，下列哪一项最能使电磁铁变强？
questions.stem_en: Safely, and with other conditions the same, which change is most likely to make an electromagnet stronger?
questions.explanation_zh: 更多匝数、更大电流、加上铁芯都会增强。选项中“增加匝数并保持合适电流”是有效做法。
questions.explanation_en: More turns, a larger current and an iron core all help. Among the options, more turns with a sensible current is an effective change.

options.zh: 把线圈拆成很少几圈，并切断电源
options.en: unwind the coil to a few turns and switch the current off

options.zh: 增加匝数，并保持合适的电流与铁芯
options.en: increase the number of turns, keeping a sensible current and the iron core

options.zh: 拿走铁芯，并把电流降到接近零
options.en: remove the core and reduce the current almost to zero

options.zh: 改用绝缘不良的裸线密绕并用水浇湿
options.en: use poorly insulated bare wire, wound tightly and made wet

questions.stem_zh: 地球周围存在着？
questions.stem_en: Around the Earth there is:
questions.explanation_zh: 地球有磁场，类似于一个巨大的条形磁体（这是一个模型）。
questions.explanation_en: The Earth has a magnetic field, similar in a simple model to that of a huge bar magnet.

options.zh: 只有电场，完全没有磁场
options.en: an electric field only, and no magnetic field

options.zh: 一层无法穿透的铁壳，所以没有磁场
options.en: an impenetrable iron shell, so no magnetic field
a vacuum wall unrelated to magnetism

questions.stem_zh: 指南针能够指示南北，主要是因为？
questions.stem_en: A compass can show north–south mainly because:
questions.explanation_zh: 小磁针在地球磁场中受力而转向，其 N 极大致指向地理北方附近（磁北）。
questions.explanation_en: The needle is a small magnet that turns in the Earth’s field; its N pole points roughly towards geographic north (magnetic north).

options.zh: 指南针内部有小型发动机
options.en: there is a small motor inside the compass

options.zh: 太阳光把指针推向南方

options.en: the Earth’s magnetic field turns the needle
the needle only swings with the wind

questions.stem_zh: 用“地球像条形磁体”的模型时，地理北极附近对应的地磁极是？
questions.stem_en: In the “Earth as a bar magnet” model, the magnetic pole near the geographic North Pole is:
questions.explanation_zh: 指南针的 N 极指向地理北方附近，说明那边相当于地磁 S 极（异名相吸）。这是学生常混的一点。
questions.explanation_en: A compass N pole points towards geographic north, so that region behaves as a magnetic S pole (unlike poles attract). This is a common mix-up.

options.zh: 地磁 S 极（所以指南针 N 极被吸向那边）
options.en: a magnetic S pole (so a compass N pole is attracted there)

options.zh: 地磁 N 极，因为地理上也叫北极
options.en: a magnetic N pole, simply because it is called north
only the centre of an electric field

questions.stem_zh: 指南针的 N 极大致指向什么方向？
questions.stem_en: Roughly which way does the N pole of a compass point?
questions.explanation_zh: 大致指向地理北方，更准确说是指向磁北方向。
questions.explanation_en: Roughly towards geographic north, or more precisely towards magnetic north.

questions.stem_zh: 地球磁场的一个重要作用是？
questions.stem_en: One important role of the Earth’s magnetic field is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 地球磁场可以偏转来自太空的带电粒子，对大气和地表环境有保护作用（第 8 阶段作定性了解即可）。
questions.explanation_en: The Earth’s field can deflect charged particles from space, giving some protection to the atmosphere and surface (a qualitative Stage 8 idea is enough).

options.en: replaces the Sun as a light source

options.zh: 有助于偏转部分来自太空的带电粒子
options.en: helps to deflect some charged particles arriving from space

questions.stem_zh: 地磁北极与地理北极？
questions.stem_en: Magnetic north and geographic north:
questions.explanation_zh: 二者接近但不完全重合，所以指南针指向的是磁北，与真北可能有夹角（磁偏角）。第 8 阶段知道它们不是同一点即可。
questions.explanation_en: They are close but not the same, so a compass points to magnetic north, which may differ from true north (magnetic declination). At Stage 8 it is enough to know they are not the same point.

options.en: are always exactly the same point

options.zh: 接近但不完全是同一点
options.en: are close but not exactly the same point
are half a world apart, always

questions.stem_zh: 在地球磁场的简单图中，磁感线在地球外部大致？
questions.stem_en: On a simple diagram of the Earth’s field, field lines outside the Earth run roughly:
questions.explanation_zh: 与条形磁体类似：在外部从地磁 N 极走向地磁 S 极。记住地理北极附近是地磁 S 极。
questions.explanation_en: As for a bar magnet: outside, they run from the magnetic N pole towards the magnetic S pole. Recall that a magnetic S pole lies near geographic north.

options.zh: 从地磁 N 极走向地磁 S 极
options.en: from the magnetic N pole towards the magnetic S pole

options.zh: 只沿赤道转圈，不进入高纬度
options.en: only in circles around the equator, never at high latitudes

options.zh: 全部指向地心，与磁极无关
options.en: all towards the Earth’s centre, unrelated to the poles

questions.stem_zh: 星系是？
questions.stem_en: A galaxy is:
questions.explanation_zh: 星系是由大量恒星、气体、尘埃等组成的巨大系统，靠引力聚集在一起。
questions.explanation_en: A galaxy is a huge system of many stars, gas and dust, held together by gravity.

options.zh: 由大量恒星、气体和尘埃组成的巨大系统
options.en: a huge system of many stars, gas and dust

options.zh: 只含一颗恒星的小石头
options.en: a small rock with only one star

questions.stem_zh: 太阳系所在的星系是？
questions.stem_en: The galaxy that contains the Solar System is:
questions.explanation_zh: 太阳和地球所在的星系是银河系（Milky Way）。
questions.explanation_en: The Sun and Earth lie in the Milky Way galaxy.

options.zh: 一个与银河系无关的小行星群，且不含太阳
options.en: an asteroid group unrelated to the Milky Way, with no Sun
a galaxy made only of Jupiter

questions.stem_zh: 从大到小，下列顺序较合理的是？
questions.stem_en: From largest to smallest, a reasonable order is:
questions.explanation_zh: 宇宙中有许多星系；一个星系含有许多恒星；一颗恒星可以拥有行星系统。太阳系属于银河系。
questions.explanation_en: The Universe contains many galaxies; a galaxy contains many stars; a star may have a planetary system. The Solar System belongs to the Milky Way.

options.zh: 星系 → 恒星（及恒星系统）→ 行星
行星 → 星系 → 恒星
一粒尘埃 → 整个宇宙 → 一颗行星
options.en: a speck of dust → the whole Universe → one planet

options.zh: 月球 → 银河系 → 一颗石子
options.en: the Moon → the Milky Way → a pebble

questions.stem_zh: 我们的太阳属于哪个星系？
questions.stem_en: Which galaxy does our Sun belong to?
questions.explanation_en: The Sun belongs to the Milky Way.

questions.stem_zh: 夜空中看到的“银河”光带，主要是？
questions.stem_en: The milky band of light sometimes seen in a dark night sky is mainly:
questions.explanation_zh: 那是我们从银河系内部侧向看去时，大量遥远恒星发出的光叠在一起。
questions.explanation_en: It is the combined light of huge numbers of distant stars, seen from inside our galaxy, looking through the disc.

options.en: the reflection of a nearby street lamp only
a crack on the Moon’s surface
the visible edge of the Earth’s magnetic field

options.zh: 银河系中大量恒星的光叠在一起
options.en: the combined light of many stars in the Milky Way

questions.stem_zh: 宇宙中星系的数量？
questions.stem_en: The number of galaxies in the Universe is:
questions.explanation_zh: 宇宙中有极多星系，银河系只是其中之一，不是唯一的星系。
questions.explanation_en: There are a great many galaxies; the Milky Way is only one of them, not the only galaxy.

options.zh: 恰好只有一个，就是银河系
非常多，银河系只是其中之一
options.en: very large; the Milky Way is only one of them

options.zh: 恰好等于太阳系中的行星数
options.en: exactly equal to the number of planets in the Solar System

questions.stem_zh: 把太阳系说成“一个星系”，错在哪里？
questions.stem_en: What is wrong with calling the Solar System “a galaxy”?
questions.explanation_zh: 太阳系是一颗恒星及其行星等天体组成的系统，规模远小于星系。星系含有极其大量的恒星。
questions.explanation_en: The Solar System is one star and its planets and other bodies, much smaller than a galaxy. A galaxy contains a vast number of stars.

options.zh: 太阳系只是一颗恒星及其周围天体，不是由大量恒星组成的星系
options.en: The Solar System is one star and the bodies around it, not a huge collection of stars

options.zh: 太阳系比任何星系都大
options.en: The Solar System is larger than any galaxy
A galaxy is smaller than one planet

options.zh: 这两个词永远可以互换
options.en: The two words can always be swapped

questions.stem_zh: 小行星通常是？
questions.stem_en: An asteroid is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 小行星是太阳系中较小的岩石（或金属）天体，大多绕太阳运行，比行星小得多。
questions.explanation_en: An asteroid is a relatively small rocky (or metallic) body in the Solar System, usually orbiting the Sun, much smaller than a planet.

options.zh: 和木星一样大的气体行星
options.en: a gas planet as large as Jupiter

options.zh: 比行星小得多的岩石或金属天体
options.en: a rocky or metallic body much smaller than a planet
a fragment of the Earth’s magnetic field

questions.stem_zh: 太阳系中许多小行星主要分布在？
questions.stem_en: Many asteroids in the Solar System are found mainly:
questions.explanation_zh: 大量小行星位于火星与木星之间的小行星带。也有其他轨道，但本阶段先记住主小行星带。
questions.explanation_en: A large number lie in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. There are other orbits too, but at this stage start with the main belt.

options.zh: 银河系以外很远、与太阳系无关的地方
options.en: far outside the Milky Way, unrelated to the Solar System

options.zh: 火星与木星之间的小行星带
options.en: in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter

questions.stem_zh: 小行星与行星相比，一个主要差别是？
questions.stem_en: Compared with a planet, a main difference is that an asteroid is typically:
questions.explanation_zh: 小行星质量、体积小得多，通常没有清理轨道，也不能像大行星那样用自身引力塑成稳定的近球形（有的近球形但仍远小于行星）。
questions.explanation_en: Asteroids are much smaller in mass and size, and they have not generally cleared their orbits. They are not large planets, even if a few are roughly rounded.

options.zh: 自己能发光，像恒星一样
options.en: able to shine by itself, like a star
not a member of the Solar System

questions.stem_zh: 主小行星带大致位于哪两颗行星之间？
questions.stem_en: Between which two planets does the main asteroid belt roughly lie?
questions.explanation_en: Between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.stem_zh: 小行星绕什么运行（主小行星带中的大多数）？
questions.stem_en: What do most asteroids in the main belt orbit?
questions.explanation_zh: 它们是太阳系的成员，大多数绕太阳运行。
questions.explanation_en: They are members of the Solar System, and most of them orbit the Sun.

options.zh: 只绕银河系中心，绝不绕太阳
options.en: only the centre of the Milky Way, never the Sun

questions.stem_zh: 偶尔有小行星的轨道靠近地球。对此较合理的认识是？
questions.stem_en: Some asteroids have orbits that come near the Earth. A reasonable view is that:
questions.explanation_zh: 近地小行星值得监测，极少数可能带来撞击风险，但不必把每一颗小行星都想象成即将撞上地球。
questions.explanation_en: Near-Earth asteroids are worth monitoring; a very small number could pose an impact risk, but it is not true that every asteroid is about to hit the Earth.

options.zh: 每一颗小行星都必定在明天撞击地球
options.en: every asteroid will certainly hit the Earth tomorrow

options.zh: 少数轨道靠近地球的天体需要监测，但不是所有小行星都会撞击地球
options.en: a few bodies that pass near Earth are monitored; not every asteroid will hit the Earth

options.zh: 小行星都在太阳内部，无法靠近地球
options.en: all asteroids are inside the Sun, so they cannot approach Earth

questions.stem_zh: 小行星与星系的关系，正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which statement about asteroids and galaxies is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 小行星是太阳系内的小天体；太阳系又位于银河系中。不要把小行星说成一个星系。
questions.explanation_en: Asteroids are small bodies in the Solar System; the Solar System itself lies in the Milky Way. An asteroid is not a galaxy.

options.zh: 小行星属于太阳系，太阳系又在星系（银河系）中
options.en: Asteroids belong to the Solar System, which itself lies in a galaxy (the Milky Way)

options.zh: 每颗小行星都是一个独立的星系
options.en: Each asteroid is a separate galaxy
A galaxy is smaller than an asteroid

options.zh: 小行星与太阳系、星系都无关
options.en: Asteroids are unrelated to the Solar System and to galaxies

questions.stem_zh: 一列火车以 $25\ \text{m/s}$ 匀速行驶 $3$ 分钟。路程是多少米？
questions.stem_en: A train travels at a steady $25\ \text{m/s}$ for $3$ minutes. How far does it go, in metres?

questions.stem_zh: 把 $54\ \text{km/h}$ 换算成 $\text{m/s}$。
questions.stem_en: Convert $54\ \text{km/h}$ into $\text{m/s}$.

questions.stem_zh: 路程—时间图像上一段水平线表示物体？
questions.stem_en: A horizontal section on a distance–time graph means the object is:
questions.explanation_zh: 路程不变，速度为零，物体静止。斜率才是速度，不是加速度。
questions.explanation_en: Distance is not changing, so the speed is zero and the object is stationary. The gradient is speed, not acceleration.

options.zh: 以很大的恒定速度运动
options.en: moving at a large constant speed

options.zh: 加速度等于这段的斜率
options.en: has acceleration equal to the gradient

questions.stem_zh: 向右 $18\ \text{N}$、向左 $7\ \text{N}$。合力大小是多少牛顿？
questions.stem_en: Forces of $18\ \text{N}$ right and $7\ \text{N}$ left. What is the size of the resultant, in newtons?
questions.explanation_en: $18-7=11\ \text{N}$ to the right. The forces are unbalanced.

questions.stem_zh: 物体沿直线做匀速运动，作用在它上面的力？
questions.stem_en: An object moves in a straight line at constant speed. The forces on it are:
questions.explanation_zh: 匀速直线运动与静止一样，合力为零，力是平衡的。
questions.explanation_en: Steady straight-line motion, like rest, means a zero resultant: the forces are balanced.

options.zh: 一定非平衡，否则它会停下
options.en: must be unbalanced, otherwise it would stop

options.zh: 不存在，因为运动中不能有力
options.en: absent, because a moving object cannot have forces

questions.stem_zh: 力 $8\ \text{N}$，垂直力臂 $1.5\ \text{m}$。力矩是多少 $\text{N\,m}$？
questions.stem_en: A force of $8\ \text{N}$ has a perpendicular distance of $1.5\ \text{m}$. What is the moment in $\text{N\,m}$?
questions.explanation_en: $M=8\times 1.5=12\ \text{N\,m}$. The distance must be perpendicular.

questions.stem_zh: $60\ \text{N}$ 的力作用在 $0.3\ \text{m}^2$ 上。压强是多少 $\text{N/m}^2$？
questions.stem_en: A $60\ \text{N}$ force acts on $0.3\ \text{m}^2$. What is the pressure in $\text{N/m}^2$?

questions.stem_zh: 气体中的扩散通常比液体中更快，主要是因为气体粒子？
questions.stem_en: Diffusion is usually faster in a gas than in a liquid mainly because gas particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 气体粒子间距更大、运动更自由。扩散来自粒子自身的无规则运动，不必搅拌。
questions.explanation_en: Gas particles are more widely spaced and move more freely. Diffusion comes from the particles’ own random motion; stirring is not required.

options.en: are more widely spaced and move more freely
can move only in a vacuum

questions.stem_zh: 一名骑行者 $12\ \text{s}$ 内前进 $90\ \text{m}$。平均速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: A cyclist travels $90\ \text{m}$ in $12\ \text{s}$. What is the average speed in $\text{m/s}$?

questions.stem_zh: 把 $18\ \text{m/s}$ 换算成 $\text{km/h}$。
questions.stem_en: Convert $18\ \text{m/s}$ into $\text{km/h}$.

questions.stem_zh: 某段路程—时间图像中，路程从 $5\ \text{m}$ 均匀增到 $29\ \text{m}$，用时 $6\ \text{s}$。速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: On a distance–time graph, distance rises steadily from $5\ \text{m}$ to $29\ \text{m}$ in $6\ \text{s}$. What is the speed in $\text{m/s}$?
questions.explanation_zh: 要用变化量：$\Delta s=24\ \text{m}$，$v=24/6=4\ \text{m/s}$。不要用 $29/6$。
questions.explanation_en: Use the change: $\Delta s=24\ \text{m}$, $v=24/6=4\ \text{m/s}$. Do not use $29/6$.

questions.stem_zh: 路程—时间图像的斜率表示？
questions.stem_en: The gradient of a distance–time graph represents:
questions.explanation_zh: 斜率是 $\Delta s/\Delta t$，即速度。加速度是速度—时间图像的斜率。
questions.explanation_en: The gradient is $\Delta s/\Delta t$, which is speed. Acceleration is the gradient of a speed–time graph.

questions.stem_zh: 书静放在桌上。正确的说法是？
questions.stem_en: A book rests on a table. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 静止说明合力为零：重力与支持力平衡，不是“不受力”。
questions.explanation_en: Being at rest means the resultant is zero: weight and the support force are balanced, not “no forces”.

options.en: No forces act on the book

options.zh: 只有重力，所以书在加速下落
options.en: Only weight acts, so the book is accelerating downwards
The resultant is upwards, so the book will rise
Weight and the support force are balanced

questions.stem_zh: 非平衡力可以？
questions.stem_en: An unbalanced force can:
questions.explanation_zh: 使物体加速、减速或改变方向。
questions.explanation_en: speed an object up, slow it down or change its direction.

options.zh: 使物体加速、减速或改变方向
options.en: speed an object up, slow it down or change its direction

options.zh: 只让物体永远保持静止
options.en: only keep an object at rest forever

questions.stem_zh: 要用 $5\ \text{N}$ 产生 $12\ \text{N\,m}$ 的力矩，垂直力臂应为多少米？
questions.stem_en: What perpendicular distance, in metres, is needed for a $5\ \text{N}$ force to give a moment of $12\ \text{N\,m}$?

questions.stem_zh: 轻质杠杆左边 $15\ \text{N}$、力臂 $0.4\ \text{m}$。右边 $6\ \text{N}$ 使之平衡，力臂是多少米？
questions.stem_en: On the left of a light lever, $15\ \text{N}$ acts $0.4\ \text{m}$ from the pivot. A $6\ \text{N}$ force on the right keeps balance. How far from the pivot is it, in metres?
questions.explanation_zh: $15\times 0.4=6\times d \Rightarrow d=1\ \text{m}$。平衡看的是力矩，不只是力相等。
questions.explanation_en: $15\times 0.4=6\times d \Rightarrow d=1\ \text{m}$. Equilibrium is about moments, not only equal forces.

questions.stem_zh: 压强为 $40\ \text{N/m}^2$，面积 $1.5\ \text{m}^2$。力是多少牛顿？
questions.stem_en: The pressure is $40\ \text{N/m}^2$ on an area of $1.5\ \text{m}^2$. What is the force in newtons?
questions.explanation_en: $F=pA=40\times 1.5=60\ \text{N}$.

questions.stem_zh: 雪地靴不容易陷进雪里，主要是因为？
questions.stem_en: Snowshoes are less likely to sink into snow mainly because they:
questions.explanation_zh: 增大面积从而减小压强，人的重力几乎不变。
questions.explanation_en: increase the area and so reduce the pressure; the person’s weight is almost unchanged.

options.en: increase the area and reduce the pressure
make the mass of the snow zero

questions.stem_zh: 体积相近时加热密闭气体，压强升高。粒子模型的解释是？
questions.stem_en: Heating a closed gas at almost constant volume raises the pressure. In the particle model this is because particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 运动更快，碰撞更频繁、更有力。压强来自各向碰撞，不只是“空气重量向下”。
questions.explanation_en: move faster, so collisions are more frequent and harder. Pressure comes from collisions in all directions, not only “the weight of air pushing down”.

options.zh: 运动更快，碰撞更频繁、更有力
options.en: move faster, so collisions are more frequent and harder
become a liquid and sink to the bottom

questions.stem_zh: 不必搅拌，色素也会在水中慢慢散开。这主要是？
questions.stem_en: A dye slowly spreads in still water with no stirring. This is mainly:
questions.explanation_zh: 液体中的扩散：粒子不断无规则运动。搅拌会加快混合，但不是扩散发生的必要条件。
questions.explanation_en: diffusion in a liquid: particles move randomly. Stirring speeds mixing but is not required for diffusion.

questions.stem_zh: 平面镜反射中，入射角为 $42^\circ$。反射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: For reflection at a plane mirror, the angle of incidence is $42^\circ$. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation_en: $i=r$, so the angle of reflection is $42^\circ$. Measure from the normal.

questions.stem_zh: 光线与镜面成 $25^\circ$。入射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: A ray makes $25^\circ$ with the mirror surface. What is the angle of incidence, in degrees?
questions.explanation_en: The angle of incidence is measured from the normal: $90^\circ-25^\circ=65^\circ$.

questions.stem_zh: 光线从空气斜射入玻璃时，通常？
questions.stem_en: A ray going from air into glass at an angle usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入更光密介质，向法线偏折。不要画成 $i=r$。
questions.explanation_en: Entering a denser medium, it bends towards the normal. Do not draw this as $i=r$.

options.zh: 反射角等于入射角后不再进入玻璃
options.en: reflects with $i=r$ and never enters the glass

options.zh: 颜色立刻变成单一紫色

questions.stem_zh: 光线从水斜射入空气时，通常？
questions.stem_en: A ray going from water into air at an angle usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入更光疏（更快）的介质，远离法线。
questions.explanation_en: Entering a less dense (faster) medium, it bends away from the normal.

questions.stem_zh: 白光通过三棱镜色散后，偏折通常最大的可见光是？
questions.stem_en: After a prism disperses white light, the visible colour usually bent most is:
questions.explanation_zh: 紫光偏折最大，红光最小。棱镜是分开原已存在的色光，不是制造颜色。
questions.explanation_en: Violet is bent most, red least. The prism separates colours already in white light; it does not create them.

questions.stem_zh: 可见光谱中，哪一种色光通过棱镜时通常偏折最小？
questions.stem_en: Which visible colour is usually bent the least by a prism?
questions.explanation_en: Red is bent the least.

questions.stem_zh: 红光与绿光适当叠加，通常得到？
questions.stem_en: Red light and green light added suitably usually give:
questions.explanation_zh: 色光加色：红+绿可得黄。不要用颜料混合的规则去套。
questions.explanation_en: Additive colour: red + green can give yellow. Do not use paint-mixing rules here.

questions.stem_zh: 白光照射只反射绿光、吸收其他可见光的物体，它看起来是？
questions.stem_en: White light falls on an object that reflects only green and absorbs other visible colours. It looks:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入眼睛的主要是被反射的绿光。
questions.explanation_en: Mainly the reflected green light reaches the eye.

options.zh: 白色，因为入射光是白的
options.en: white, because the incoming light is white

options.zh: 一定是黑色，因为有光被吸收
options.en: black for sure, because some light is absorbed

questions.stem_zh: 写出平面镜的反射定律（可写 $i=r$ 并说明从哪量角）。
questions.stem_en: State the law of reflection at a plane surface (you may write $i=r$ and say how the angles are measured).
questions.explanation_zh: 入射角等于反射角，二者都从法线量起；入射光线、法线、反射光线共面。
questions.explanation_en: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal; the incident ray, normal and reflected ray are coplanar.
accepted: angle of incidence equals angle of reflection

questions.stem_zh: 入射角为 $28^\circ$。反射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: The angle of incidence is $28^\circ$. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation_en: $i=r=28^\circ$.

questions.stem_zh: 光线与镜面成 $40^\circ$。反射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: A ray makes $40^\circ$ with the mirror. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation_en: Angle of incidence $=90^\circ-40^\circ=50^\circ$, so the angle of reflection is also $50^\circ$.

questions.stem_zh: 入射角、反射角必须从哪一条线量起？
questions.stem_en: The angles of incidence and reflection must be measured from:
questions.explanation_en: the normal, not the mirror surface.

options.en: the line from the lamp to the eye

questions.stem_zh: 光线从空气斜射入水面，通常会？
questions.stem_en: A ray going from air into water at an angle usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 进入更光密介质，向法线偏折。空气—水与空气—玻璃规则相同。
questions.explanation_en: Entering a denser medium, it bends towards the normal. The same rule holds for air–water and air–glass.

questions.stem_zh: 光线沿法线从空气进入玻璃，方向会怎样？
questions.stem_en: A ray travels from air into glass along the normal. What happens to its direction?
questions.explanation_zh: 不偏折，方向不变（在玻璃中会变慢）。
questions.explanation_en: No bending: the direction stays the same (though the light slows in the glass).

questions.stem_zh: 池底看起来比实际浅，一个原因是？
questions.stem_en: A pool can look shallower than it is. One reason is:
questions.explanation_zh: 从水中射出的光线在水面远离法线，沿直线追迹会觉得池底被抬高。
questions.explanation_en: Rays leaving the water bend away from the normal; tracing them back in straight lines raises the apparent bottom.

options.zh: 水中射出的光线远离法线，池底的像被抬高
options.en: rays leaving the water bend away from the normal, raising the image of the bottom

options.zh: 水把所有光反射回太阳
options.en: the water reflects all light back to the Sun
the law of reflection has failed
it is only to do with asteroids

questions.stem_zh: 白光色散说明白光？
questions.stem_en: Dispersion of white light shows that white light:
questions.explanation_zh: 由多种色光组成。棱镜将它们分开，而不是制造新颜色。
questions.explanation_en: is a mixture of colours. The prism separates them; it does not create new colours.

options.zh: 是单一颜色，颜色由棱镜制造
options.en: is a single colour, and the prism creates the others
is the same process as diffusion
is made up of a range of colours

questions.stem_zh: 棱镜光谱中，红光与紫光相比通常？
questions.stem_en: In a prism spectrum, red light compared with violet is usually:
questions.explanation_en: bent less than violet.

options.en: does not pass through the prism at all

questions.stem_zh: 红、绿、蓝三束色光适当叠加可以得到？
questions.stem_en: Red, green and blue light added suitably can give:
questions.explanation_zh: 加色三原色会合可得白光。
questions.explanation_en: the additive primaries can combine to give white light.

questions.stem_zh: 只用蓝光照射一块只能反射红光（吸收蓝光）的物体，它看起来最可能？
questions.stem_en: Blue light alone falls on an object that can reflect only red (and absorbs blue). It is most likely to look:
questions.explanation_zh: 没有可反射的红光，蓝光又被吸收，看起来很暗或接近黑色。颜色与照明有关。
questions.explanation_en: There is no red to reflect and the blue is absorbed, so it looks very dark or nearly black. Colour depends on the lighting.

questions.stem_zh: 条形磁体外部的磁感线通常？
questions.stem_en: Field lines outside a bar magnet usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 从 N 极出发回到 S 极。线条是模型，不是真实绳子；越密表示越强。
questions.explanation_en: leave the N pole and return to the S pole. The lines are a model, not real strings; closer lines mean a stronger field.

options.zh: 从 N 极出发，回到 S 极
options.en: leave N and return to S

options.zh: 从 S 极出发，回到 N 极
options.en: leave S and return to N

questions.stem_zh: 磁感线画得更密的地方，磁场通常？
questions.stem_en: Where field lines are closer together, the field is usually:
questions.explanation_en: stronger, for example near the poles.

questions.stem_zh: 用什么简单仪器可以显示磁场的方向？
questions.stem_en: What simple instrument can show the direction of a magnetic field?
questions.explanation_en: A plotting compass.

questions.stem_zh: 电磁铁的一个重要优点是？
questions.stem_en: An important advantage of an electromagnet is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 可以通过通断电来开关磁性，便于放下工件。
questions.explanation_en: can be switched on and off with the current, so a load can be dropped.

options.en: can be switched on and off with the current
can only be used for dispersion

questions.stem_zh: 断开电流后，电磁铁通常会？
questions.stem_en: When the current is switched off, an electromagnet usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁性大大减弱或消失，可以放下被吸住的铁质物体。
questions.explanation_en: lose most or all of its magnetism, so a lifted iron object can be released.

options.zh: 变得更强且无法放下工件
options.en: become stronger and unable to release a load

options.zh: 磁性减弱或消失，可放下工件
options.en: lose magnetism and can drop a load

questions.stem_zh: 其他条件相近时，增加匝数通常使电磁铁？
questions.stem_en: If other conditions are similar, more turns usually make an electromagnet:
questions.explanation_zh: 更强。电流增大、加上铁芯也会增强。比较时一次只改一个因素。
questions.explanation_en: stronger. A larger current or an iron core also helps. Change one factor at a time in a fair test.

questions.stem_zh: 列出两个能使电磁铁更强的因素。
questions.stem_en: Name two factors that can make an electromagnet stronger.
questions.explanation_zh: 更大电流、更多匝数、加上铁芯，答出两个即可。
questions.explanation_en: A larger current, more turns, or an iron core — any two.

questions.stem_zh: 比较匝数的影响时，公平实验应？
questions.stem_en: In a fair test of the number of turns you should:
questions.explanation_zh: 只改变匝数，控制电流、铁芯等其他变量。
questions.explanation_en: change only the number of turns and control current, core and other variables.

options.zh: 同时随意改电流和铁芯
options.en: also change current and core at random

options.zh: 只改变匝数，控制其他变量
options.en: change only the turns and control other variables

questions.stem_zh: 磁场是？
questions.stem_en: A magnetic field is:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁体周围有磁力作用的空间。
questions.explanation_en: the region around a magnet where magnetic forces act.

options.zh: 只有声音才能通过的区域
options.en: a region that only sound can pass through

options.zh: 磁体周围有磁力作用的空间
options.en: the region around a magnet where magnetic forces act

questions.stem_zh: 两个磁极靠近时？
questions.stem_en: When two magnetic poles are brought close:
questions.explanation_en: like poles repel and unlike poles attract.

options.en: like poles repel and unlike attract
like poles attract and unlike repel

questions.stem_zh: 小磁针的 N 极指向该处磁场的？
questions.stem_en: The N pole of a plotting compass points in the direction of:
questions.explanation_zh: 该点磁场的方向（磁体外磁感线从 N 到 S）。
questions.explanation_en: the field at that point (outside a magnet, lines run from N to S).

options.en: the magnetic field at that point
the direction of a sound wave

options.zh: 任意随机方向，没有规则
options.en: a random direction with no rule

questions.stem_zh: 磁感线是？
questions.stem_en: Magnetic field lines are:
questions.explanation_zh: 描述方向和相对强弱的图示模型，不是实物。
questions.explanation_en: a diagram model for direction and relative strength, not real objects.

options.en: iron wires you can pick up

options.zh: 表示方向和强弱的模型图线
options.en: model lines showing direction and strength

questions.stem_zh: 最简单的电磁铁通常包括？
questions.stem_en: The simplest electromagnet usually includes:
questions.explanation_zh: 绕在铁芯上的绝缘线圈，并通以电流。
questions.explanation_en: an insulated coil on an iron core, with a current in the coil.

options.en: an iron core, an insulated coil and a current

options.zh: 只有一块不能关断的永磁体
options.en: only a permanent magnet that cannot be switched off

questions.stem_zh: 铁芯的主要作用是？
questions.stem_en: The main job of the iron core is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 增强并集中磁场。常用软铁，以便断电后迅速退磁。
questions.explanation_en: strengthen and concentrate the field. Soft iron is used so that it demagnetises quickly when the current stops.

questions.stem_zh: 电磁铁可用于？
questions.stem_en: Electromagnets can be used in:
questions.explanation_zh: 起重、电铃、继电器等需要可开关磁性的装置。
questions.explanation_en: lifting magnets, bells, relays and other devices that need switchable magnetism.

options.zh: 可开关的起重、电铃、继电器等
测量星系的质量（本课范围）

questions.stem_zh: 其他条件相近时，增大电流通常使电磁铁？
questions.stem_en: If other conditions are similar, a larger current usually makes an electromagnet:
questions.explanation_zh: 更强。但电流过大导致过热会既不安全也不再公平。
questions.explanation_en: stronger. A current so large that the wire overheats is unsafe and may spoil a fair test.

questions.stem_zh: 有铁芯的线圈与空心线圈相比（其他条件相近）通常？
questions.stem_en: A coil with an iron core, compared with an air-cored coil (other conditions similar), is usually:
questions.explanation_en: stronger.

options.zh: 不能吸起任何铁质物体

questions.stem_zh: 电流过大、导线明显发热时，主要问题是？
questions.stem_en: If a very large current makes the wire heat up badly, a main problem is:
questions.explanation_zh: 不安全，且可能改变电阻、损坏绝缘，实验不再公平。
questions.explanation_en: it can be unsafe, and it may change the resistance or damage insulation, so the test is no longer fair.

options.zh: 发热证明电磁铁一定变弱
options.en: heating proves the electromagnet must be weaker

options.zh: 不安全，实验也可能不再公平
options.en: it may be unsafe, and the test may no longer be fair

options.zh: 发热完全有益，应继续加大电流
options.en: heating is entirely helpful, so increase the current further

options.zh: 这时应浇水并继续通大电流
options.en: pour water on it and keep a large current flowing

questions.stem_zh: 为什么电磁铁的线圈常用绝缘导线？
questions.stem_en: Why is the wire of an electromagnet usually insulated?
questions.explanation_zh: 防止相邻圈短路，电流才能一圈圈绕过铁芯。
questions.explanation_en: To prevent neighbouring turns shorting, so the current can travel around the core turn by turn.

questions.stem_zh: 指南针能指示南北，主要是因为？
questions.stem_en: A compass shows north–south mainly because:
questions.explanation_zh: 小磁针在地球磁场中转向。
questions.explanation_en: the needle is a small magnet that turns in the Earth’s magnetic field.

options.en: there is a motor inside the needle
the Earth’s magnetic field turns the needle
it only swings with the wind

questions.stem_zh: 地理北极附近，在“地球像条形磁体”的模型中相当于？
questions.stem_en: In the bar-magnet model of the Earth, the region near geographic north behaves as:
questions.explanation_zh: 地磁 S 极，因为指南针 N 极被吸向那边。
questions.explanation_en: a magnetic S pole, because a compass N pole is attracted there.

options.zh: 地磁 N 极，只因名称里有“北”
options.en: a magnetic N pole, only because it is called north

questions.stem_zh: 指南针的 N 极大致指向什么方向？
questions.stem_en: Roughly which way does a compass N pole point?
questions.explanation_zh: 大致指向地理北方或磁北。
questions.explanation_en: Roughly geographic north, or magnetic north.

questions.stem_zh: 太阳系位于哪个星系？
questions.stem_en: The Solar System lies in which galaxy?
questions.explanation_zh: 银河系。太阳系本身不是一个星系。
questions.explanation_en: the Milky Way. The Solar System itself is not a galaxy.

options.en: it is a galaxy by itself

questions.stem_zh: 星系是？
questions.stem_en: A galaxy is:
questions.explanation_zh: 由大量恒星、气体和尘埃组成的巨大系统。
questions.explanation_en: a huge system of many stars, gas and dust.

options.zh: 由大量恒星、气体和尘埃组成的巨大系统
options.en: a huge system of many stars, gas and dust

questions.stem_zh: 许多小行星主要分布在？
questions.stem_en: Many asteroids are found mainly:
questions.explanation_zh: 火星与木星之间的小行星带。它们绕太阳运行，比行星小得多。
questions.explanation_en: in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter. They orbit the Sun and are much smaller than planets.

options.zh: 火星与木星之间的小行星带
options.en: in the asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter

options.zh: 银河系以外且与太阳系无关
options.en: outside the Milky Way, unrelated to the Solar System

questions.stem_zh: 主小行星带大致位于哪两颗行星之间？
questions.stem_en: Between which two planets does the main asteroid belt lie?
questions.explanation_en: Between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.stem_zh: 小行星与星系的关系，正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which statement about asteroids and galaxies is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 小行星属于太阳系，太阳系又在银河系中。不要把小行星叫做星系。
questions.explanation_en: Asteroids belong to the Solar System, which lies in the Milky Way. An asteroid is not a galaxy.

options.zh: 小行星属于太阳系，太阳系位于星系中
options.en: Asteroids belong to the Solar System, which lies in a galaxy

options.zh: 每颗小行星都是一个星系

options.en: A galaxy is smaller than an asteroid

questions.stem_zh: 地球周围存在着？
questions.stem_en: Around the Earth there is:
questions.explanation_zh: 磁场，可用巨型条形磁体作简单模型。
questions.explanation_en: a magnetic field, modelled simply as a huge bar magnet.

options.en: an electric field only, and no magnetic field

options.zh: 一层完全隔绝磁力的墙
options.en: a wall that completely blocks magnetism
a vacuum shell unrelated to magnetism

questions.stem_zh: 磁北与地理北极？
questions.stem_en: Magnetic north and the geographic North Pole:
questions.explanation_zh: 接近但不完全是同一点。
questions.explanation_en: are close but not exactly the same point.

options.en: are always half a world apart
are close but not exactly the same

questions.stem_zh: 地球磁场的一个作用是？
questions.stem_en: One role of the Earth’s magnetic field is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 有助于偏转部分来自太空的带电粒子。
questions.explanation_en: helps to deflect some charged particles arriving from space.

options.zh: 有助于偏转部分来自太空的带电粒子
options.en: helps to deflect some charged particles from space
replaces the Sun as a light source

questions.stem_zh: 指南针 N 极指向地理北方附近，说明那边相当于？
questions.stem_en: A compass N pole points towards geographic north, which means that region acts as:
questions.explanation_zh: 地磁 S 极（异名相吸）。这是常见易错点。
questions.explanation_en: a magnetic S pole (unlike poles attract). This is a common pitfall.

questions.stem_zh: 我们的太阳属于哪个星系？
questions.stem_en: Which galaxy does our Sun belong to?
questions.explanation_en: The Milky Way.

questions.stem_zh: 从大到小，较合理的顺序是？
questions.stem_en: From largest to smallest, a reasonable order is:
questions.explanation_zh: 星系 → 恒星系统 → 行星。
questions.explanation_en: galaxy → star system → planet.

options.zh: 行星 → 星系 → 恒星
星系 → 恒星（及恒星系统）→ 行星
月球 → 银河系 → 石子
options.en: the Moon → the Milky Way → a pebble

options.zh: 一粒尘埃 → 宇宙 → 一颗行星
options.en: a dust grain → the Universe → one planet

questions.stem_zh: 宇宙中星系的数量？
questions.stem_en: The number of galaxies in the Universe is:
questions.explanation_zh: 非常多，银河系只是其中之一。
questions.explanation_en: very large; the Milky Way is only one of them.

options.zh: 非常多，银河系只是其中之一
options.en: very large; the Milky Way is only one of them

options.zh: 恰好等于太阳系行星数
options.en: exactly the number of planets in the Solar System

questions.stem_zh: 把太阳系称为“一个星系”，错在哪里？
questions.stem_en: What is wrong with calling the Solar System a galaxy?
questions.explanation_zh: 太阳系只有一颗恒星及其周围天体，远小于由大量恒星组成的星系。
questions.explanation_en: The Solar System is one star and the bodies around it, much smaller than a galaxy of many stars.

options.zh: 太阳系比任何星系都大
