options.en: The Solar System is larger than any galaxy

options.zh: 这两个词永远可以互换
options.en: The two words can always be swapped

options.zh: 太阳系不是由大量恒星组成的系统
options.en: The Solar System is not a huge collection of stars
A galaxy is smaller than a planet

questions.stem_zh: 小行星通常是？
questions.stem_en: An asteroid is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 比行星小得多的岩石或金属天体，大多绕太阳运行。
questions.explanation_en: a rocky or metallic body much smaller than a planet, usually orbiting the Sun.

options.zh: 和木星一样大的气体行星
options.en: a gas planet as large as Jupiter

options.zh: 比行星小得多的岩石或金属天体
options.en: a rocky or metallic body much smaller than a planet
a fragment of the Earth’s magnetic field

questions.stem_zh: 主小行星带中的大多数小行星绕什么运行？
questions.stem_en: Most asteroids in the main belt orbit:
questions.explanation_en: the Sun.

options.zh: 只绕银河系中心且绝不绕太阳
options.en: only the centre of the Milky Way, never the Sun

questions.stem_zh: 关于近地小行星，较合理的说法是？
questions.stem_en: A reasonable statement about near-Earth asteroids is:
questions.explanation_zh: 少数轨道靠近地球的天体需要监测，但不是每一颗小行星都会撞击地球。
questions.explanation_en: a few bodies that pass near Earth are monitored; not every asteroid will hit the Earth.

options.zh: 少数靠近地球的天体需要监测，并非所有小行星都会撞击地球
options.en: a few near-Earth bodies are monitored; not every asteroid will hit Earth

options.zh: 每一颗都必定在明天撞击地球
options.en: every one will certainly hit the Earth tomorrow
they all lie inside the Sun

questions.stem_zh: 一辆汽车 $8\ \text{s}$ 内前进 $96\ \text{m}$。平均速度是多少 $\text{m/s}$？
questions.stem_en: A car travels $96\ \text{m}$ in $8\ \text{s}$. What is its average speed in $\text{m/s}$?

questions.stem_zh: 把 $90\ \text{km/h}$ 换算成 $\text{m/s}$。
questions.stem_en: Convert $90\ \text{km/h}$ into $\text{m/s}$.

questions.stem_zh: 路程—时间图像上更陡的直线通常表示？
questions.stem_en: A steeper straight line on a distance–time graph usually means:
questions.explanation_zh: 斜率是速度，更陡表示恒定速度更大，不是加速度。
questions.explanation_en: The gradient is speed; a steeper line means a greater constant speed, not acceleration.

questions.stem_zh: 合力为零时，物体将会？
questions.stem_en: When the resultant force is zero, an object will:
questions.explanation_zh: 保持静止或匀速直线运动。静止不等于不受力。
questions.explanation_en: stay at rest or keep a constant speed in a straight line. Rest does not mean “no forces”.

options.zh: 保持静止或匀速直线运动
options.en: stay at rest or keep a steady speed in a straight line

questions.stem_zh: $20\ \text{N}$ 的力，垂直力臂 $0.3\ \text{m}$。力矩是多少 $\text{N\,m}$？
questions.stem_en: A $20\ \text{N}$ force has a perpendicular distance of $0.3\ \text{m}$. What is the moment in $\text{N\,m}$?
questions.explanation_en: $M=20\times 0.3=6\ \text{N\,m}$. Use the perpendicular distance.

questions.stem_zh: $45\ \text{N}$ 作用在 $0.9\ \text{m}^2$ 上。压强是多少 $\text{N/m}^2$？
questions.stem_en: A $45\ \text{N}$ force acts on $0.9\ \text{m}^2$. What is the pressure in $\text{N/m}^2$?
questions.explanation_en: $p=45/0.9=50\ \text{N/m}^2$. Do not confuse this with the moment unit $\text{N\,m}$.

questions.stem_zh: 气体压强主要来自粒子？
questions.stem_en: Gas pressure is mainly due to particles:
questions.explanation_zh: 不断碰撞器壁。封闭气体对各个方向的器壁都有压强。
questions.explanation_en: colliding continually with the walls. A trapped gas pushes on every wall, not only downwards.

options.en: all sitting still at the bottom

options.zh: 只有重量向下，侧面不受力
options.en: their weight only, so the sides feel no force

questions.stem_zh: 光线与平面镜成 $20^\circ$。反射角是多少度？
questions.stem_en: A ray makes $20^\circ$ with a plane mirror. What is the angle of reflection, in degrees?
questions.explanation_zh: 入射角 $=90^\circ-20^\circ=70^\circ$，故 $r=70^\circ$。不要把 $20^\circ$ 当成入射角。
questions.explanation_en: Angle of incidence $=90^\circ-20^\circ=70^\circ$, so $r=70^\circ$. Do not treat $20^\circ$ as the angle of incidence.

questions.stem_zh: 光线从空气斜射入玻璃，通常会？
questions.stem_en: A ray going from air into glass at an angle usually:
questions.explanation_en: bends towards the normal. Refraction is not $i=r$.

options.zh: 反射角等于入射角且不再进入玻璃
options.en: reflects with $i=r$ and never enters the glass

questions.stem_zh: 白光通过棱镜色散时，偏折通常最小的可见光是？
questions.stem_en: When a prism disperses white light, the visible colour usually bent least is:
questions.explanation_zh: 红光偏折最小，紫光最大。棱镜分开原已存在的色光。
questions.explanation_en: Red is bent least, violet most. The prism separates colours already present in white light.

questions.stem_zh: 红光加绿光适当叠加通常得到黄光。这与红、绿颜料混合常常不同，因为？
questions.stem_en: Red light plus green light can give yellow. This often differs from mixing red and green paints because:
questions.explanation_zh: 色光是加色，颜料更多地是减色（吸收）。
questions.explanation_en: lights add (additive colour); paints mainly absorb (subtractive colour).

options.zh: 二者结果永远完全一样
颜料会发光而色光只会吸收
options.en: paints emit light while coloured light only absorbs

options.zh: 色光是叠加（加色），颜料更多是吸收（减色）
只有颜料遵守反射定律
options.en: only paints obey the law of reflection

questions.stem_zh: 条形磁体外部的磁感线从哪一极指向哪一极？
questions.stem_en: Outside a bar magnet, field lines run from which pole to which pole?
questions.explanation_zh: 从 N 到 S。线条越密磁场越强。
questions.explanation_en: From N to S. Closer lines mean a stronger field.

questions.stem_zh: 使电磁铁更强的一个有效做法是（在安全前提下）？
questions.stem_en: One effective way to make an electromagnet stronger (safely) is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 增加匝数、适当增大电流，或使用铁芯。断电后磁性可减弱以便放下工件。
questions.explanation_en: increase the number of turns, increase the current sensibly, or use an iron core. Switching off lets the magnetism fall so a load can be dropped.

options.en: switch the current off and remove the core

options.zh: 增加匝数（并保持合适电流与铁芯）
options.en: increase the number of turns (keeping a sensible current and the core)

options.zh: 改用塑料芯并尽量减少匝数
options.en: use a plastic core and as few turns as possible
wind bare wire tightly and make it wet

questions.stem_zh: 指南针 N 极指向地理北方附近，说明该处相当于？
questions.stem_en: A compass N pole points towards geographic north, so that region acts as:
questions.explanation_zh: 地磁 S 极。磁北与真北接近但不完全重合。
questions.explanation_en: a magnetic S pole. Magnetic north and true north are close but not the same.

questions.stem_zh: 下列说法正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 太阳系位于银河系；许多小行星在火星与木星之间绕太阳运行。不要把太阳系或小行星叫做星系。
questions.explanation_en: The Solar System lies in the Milky Way; many asteroids orbit the Sun between Mars and Jupiter. Do not call the Solar System or an asteroid a galaxy.

options.zh: 太阳系位于银河系，小行星是太阳系中较小的天体
options.en: The Solar System lies in the Milky Way; asteroids are smaller bodies in the Solar System

options.zh: 太阳系本身就是一个星系，小行星则是更大的星系
options.en: The Solar System is itself a galaxy, and each asteroid is a larger galaxy

options.zh: 小行星带位于太阳内部
options.en: The asteroid belt lies inside the Sun

options.zh: 宇宙中只有银河系一个星系
options.en: The Milky Way is the only galaxy in the Universe

questions.stem_zh: 卢瑟福模型认为原子的质量几乎全部位于？
questions.stem_en: In the Rutherford model, almost all the mass of an atom is in the:
questions.explanation_zh: 质量几乎全部在很小的原子核里。
questions.explanation_en: Almost all the mass is in the tiny nucleus.

options.zh: 电子云的最外沿且电子最重
options.en: the outer edge, because electrons are the heaviest
a shell made only of neutrons

questions.stem_zh: 大多数α粒子几乎直线穿过金箔，主要因为？
questions.stem_en: Most alpha particles go almost straight through gold foil mainly because:
questions.explanation_en: An atom is mostly empty space.

options.zh: 电子把所有α粒子吸住后又放行
options.en: electrons catch every alpha particle and then release it

questions.stem_zh: 质子、中子、电子的相对电荷依次是？
questions.stem_en: The relative charges of a proton, a neutron and an electron are:
questions.explanation_en: Proton $+1$, neutron $0$, electron $-1$.

questions.stem_zh: 某中性原子有 $12$ 个质子和 $12$ 个中子。电子数是多少？
questions.stem_en: A neutral atom has $12$ protons and $12$ neutrons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation_zh: 中性原子电子数等于质子数，为 $12$。中子不影响电荷。
questions.explanation_en: In a neutral atom, electrons equal protons, so $12$. Neutrons do not affect charge.

questions.stem_zh: 电子被留在核周围，是因为？
questions.stem_en: Electrons are held around the nucleus because:
questions.explanation_zh: 核带正电、电子带负电，异种电荷相吸。
questions.explanation_en: The nucleus is positive and electrons are negative, so opposite charges attract.

options.en: electrons are heavier than the nucleus

questions.stem_zh: 判断固体是否纯，常用的证据是？
questions.stem_en: A useful piece of evidence for whether a solid is pure is:
questions.explanation_zh: 纯净物有尖锐、固定的熔点，可与数据手册比较。
questions.explanation_en: A pure substance has a sharp, fixed melting point that can be compared with a data book.

options.zh: 测定熔点并与数据比较
options.en: measure the melting point and compare it with data
only check whether the colour looks bright

options.zh: 称一次质量即可，不必看温度
options.en: weigh it once; temperature is irrelevant

options.zh: 看它是否含有超过一种元素——化合物都不是纯净物
options.en: see if it contains more than one element — compounds are never pure

questions.stem_zh: 杂质对固体熔点的典型影响是？
questions.stem_en: Impurities typically affect the melting point of a solid by:
questions.explanation_zh: 通常使熔点降低、熔程变宽。
questions.explanation_en: They usually lower it and widen the range.

options.en: raising it and making it sharper

options.zh: 使熔点降低且熔程变宽
options.en: lowering it and widening the range

questions.stem_zh: 同种电荷之间是相吸还是相斥？
questions.stem_en: Do like charges attract or repel?
questions.explanation_en: Like charges repel; opposite charges attract.
questions.answer_zh: 相斥。
questions.answer_en: They repel.

questions.stem_zh: 少数α粒子发生大角度偏转，说明原子核？
questions.stem_en: A few alpha particles are deflected through large angles. This shows that the nucleus is:
questions.explanation_zh: 正电荷和质量集中在很小的、质量很大的核上。
questions.explanation_en: Positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny, massive nucleus.

options.en: large enough to fill the atom

options.zh: 很小且集中了正电荷和质量
options.en: tiny, with concentrated positive charge and mass

questions.stem_zh: 卢瑟福模型中，电子位于？
questions.stem_en: In the Rutherford model, electrons are located:
questions.explanation_zh: 电子在原子核周围的空间中。
questions.explanation_en: Electrons occupy the space around the nucleus.

options.en: in the space around the nucleus
all on the surface of the gold foil

questions.stem_zh: 中子的相对电荷和相对质量（近似）分别是？
questions.stem_en: A neutron’s relative charge and approximate relative mass are:
questions.explanation_en: Charge $0$ and relative mass about $1$.

questions.stem_zh: 中性原子有 $9$ 个质子。电子数是多少？
questions.stem_en: A neutral atom has $9$ protons. How many electrons does it have?
questions.explanation_zh: 中性原子电子数等于质子数。
questions.explanation_en: In a neutral atom, electrons equal protons.

questions.stem_zh: α粒子被核推开，是因为？
questions.stem_en: An alpha particle is pushed away from a nucleus because:
questions.explanation_zh: 两者都带正电，同种电荷相斥。
questions.explanation_en: Both are positive, so like charges repel.

options.zh: 两者都带正电，同种相斥
options.en: both are positive, so like charges repel

questions.stem_zh: 把电子留在原子里的力是？
questions.stem_en: The force that holds electrons in the atom is:
questions.explanation_zh: 核与电子之间的静电引力。
questions.explanation_en: Electrostatic attraction between the nucleus and the electrons.

questions.stem_zh: 下列哪一种是混合物？
questions.stem_en: Which of these is a mixture?
questions.explanation_zh: 空气含有多种气体，是混合物；蒸馏水和纯二氧化碳是纯净物。
questions.explanation_en: Air contains several gases, so it is a mixture; distilled water and pure carbon dioxide are pure substances.

options.zh: 只由一种元素组成的样品
options.en: a sample that is a single element

questions.stem_zh: 某固体数据熔点为 $120^\circ\mathrm{C}$，样品在 $110$–$118^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 熔化。较合理的结论是？
questions.stem_en: A solid should melt at $120^\circ\mathrm{C}$, but a sample melts from $110$ to $118^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A reasonable conclusion is:
questions.explanation_zh: 熔点偏低且熔程宽，样品可能不纯。
questions.explanation_en: The melting point is low and the range is wide, so the sample may be impure.

options.en: the sample must be purer than the data-book substance
the sample must be a gas

questions.stem_zh: 为什么中性原子整体电荷为零？
questions.stem_en: Why is the overall charge of a neutral atom zero?
questions.explanation_en: Neutrons do not contribute charge.
accepted: 质子与电子数目相等，电荷抵消
questions.answer_zh: 质子数等于电子数，正负电荷抵消。
questions.answer_en: The numbers of protons and electrons are equal, so the charges cancel.

questions.stem_zh: 若原子是带均匀正电的实心球，α粒子散射最可能怎样？
questions.stem_en: If atoms were solid balls of spread-out positive charge, alpha scattering would most likely show:
questions.explanation_zh: 不会出现少数非常大的偏转，因为没有又小又集中的核。
questions.explanation_en: There would not be a few very large deflections, because there would be no tiny concentrated nucleus.

options.en: even more particles bouncing almost straight back

options.zh: 几乎只有小角度偏转，很少有极大偏转
options.en: only small deflections, with very few huge ones

options.zh: 所有粒子都停在箔的表面
options.en: every particle stopping on the surface of the foil
all electrons falling into the nucleus

questions.stem_zh: 纯净物的沸点通常是？
questions.stem_en: The boiling point of a pure substance is usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 纯净物有固定、尖锐的沸点。
questions.explanation_en: A pure substance has a sharp, fixed boiling point.

options.zh: 一定比所有混合物都低很多且无范围可言
options.en: always far lower than any mixture, with no range idea

questions.stem_zh: 中子不提供核与电子之间的静电吸引，因为中子？
questions.stem_en: Neutrons do not provide the electrostatic attraction between the nucleus and electrons because they:
questions.explanation_en: Neutrons are uncharged.

questions.stem_zh: $10\ \mathrm{g}$ 溶质配成 $0.25\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ 溶液。浓度是多少 $\mathrm{g/dm^3}$？
questions.stem_en: $10\ \mathrm{g}$ of solute is made up to $0.25\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ of solution. Concentration in $\mathrm{g/dm^3}$?

questions.stem_zh: $5.0\ \mathrm{g}$ 溶质配成 $200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ 溶液。浓度是多少 $\mathrm{g/dm^3}$？
questions.stem_en: $5.0\ \mathrm{g}$ of solute is made up to $200\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ of solution. Concentration in $\mathrm{g/dm^3}$?

questions.stem_zh: 加水稀释溶液（溶质质量不变）时，浓度？
questions.stem_en: When a solution is diluted with water (mass of solute unchanged), concentration:
questions.explanation_en: The volume increases, so the concentration falls.

questions.stem_zh: 溶剂移动 $8.0\ \mathrm{cm}$，斑点移动 $2.0\ \mathrm{cm}$。$R_f$ 是多少？
questions.stem_en: The solvent travels $8.0\ \mathrm{cm}$ and a spot travels $2.0\ \mathrm{cm}$. What is $R_f$?

questions.stem_zh: 纸层析中，起点线应在溶剂液面的？
questions.stem_en: In paper chromatography, the baseline should be:
questions.explanation_zh: 起点线要在液面上方，以免样品被洗掉。
questions.explanation_en: The baseline must sit above the solvent surface so the sample is not washed off.

options.en: on the bench outside the beaker

options.zh: 溶剂前沿的上面且先于实验划上墨水
options.en: above the solvent front, already drawn in ink

questions.stem_zh: 两个斑点说明样品？
questions.stem_en: Two spots suggest that the sample:
questions.explanation_zh: 至少含有两种可被分开的成分，是混合物。
questions.explanation_en: Contains at least two substances that can be separated, so it is a mixture.

options.zh: 实验失败，因为纯净物必须有两个斑点
options.en: failed, because a pure substance must show two spots

questions.stem_zh: $1\ \mathrm{dm^3}$ 等于多少 $\mathrm{cm^3}$？
questions.stem_en: How many $\mathrm{cm^3}$ are there in $1\ \mathrm{dm^3}$?
questions.explanation_en: $1\ \mathrm{dm^3}=1000\ \mathrm{cm^3}=1\ \mathrm{L}$.

questions.stem_zh: 比较 $R_f$ 来鉴定物质时，必须？
questions.stem_en: To identify a substance by comparing $R_f$ values, you must:
questions.explanation_zh: 在相同条件（溶剂、温度等）下与已知样品比较。
questions.explanation_en: Compare with a known sample under the same conditions (solvent, temperature and so on).

options.zh: 改用完全不同的溶剂却直接比较数字
options.en: change the solvent completely and still compare the numbers directly

options.zh: 在相同条件下与已知物质比较
options.en: compare with a known substance under the same conditions

questions.stem_zh: 浓度为 $15\ \mathrm{g/dm^3}$ 的溶液有 $0.80\ \mathrm{dm^3}$。溶质质量是多少克？
questions.stem_en: A solution of concentration $15\ \mathrm{g/dm^3}$ has volume $0.80\ \mathrm{dm^3}$. Mass of solute in grams?
questions.explanation_en: $15\times 0.80=12\ \mathrm{g}$.

questions.stem_zh: $9.0\ \mathrm{g}$ 溶质配成 $500\ \mathrm{cm^3}$ 溶液。浓度是多少 $\mathrm{g/dm^3}$？

questions.stem_zh: 氢气在氧气中燃烧生成水。写出文字方程式。
questions.stem_en: Hydrogen burns in oxygen to form water. Write the word equation.
questions.explanation_zh: 不要把水写在箭头左边。
questions.explanation_en: Do not put water on the left of the arrow.
questions.answer_zh: 氢气 $+$ 氧气 $\rightarrow$ 水
questions.answer_en: hydrogen $+$ oxygen $\rightarrow$ water

questions.stem_zh: 下列说法正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 化学反应中原子重新组合成新物质；文字方程式用名称记录这一过程。
questions.explanation_en: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged into new substances; a word equation records this with names.

options.zh: 文字方程式的箭头可以随意反向，意义不变
options.en: you can reverse the arrow with no change of meaning

options.zh: 反应物就是新生成的物质
options.en: reactants are the new substances formed

options.zh: 文字方程式必须写出电子电荷
options.en: a word equation must show electron charges

options.zh: 反应物变成新的生成物，用箭头表示这个方向
options.en: reactants form new products; the arrow shows that direction

questions.stem_zh: 放热过程中，周围的温度通常？
questions.stem_en: In an exothermic process, the temperature of the surroundings usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 放热向周围释放能量，周围温度升高。
questions.explanation_en: Energy is released to the surroundings, so their temperature rises.

questions.stem_zh: 某盐溶于水后烧杯外壁变凉。这个过程是？
questions.stem_en: A salt dissolves in water and the outside of the beaker feels colder. The process is:
questions.explanation_zh: 周围温度降低，说明过程从周围吸能，是吸热。
questions.explanation_en: The surroundings get colder, so the process takes in energy: it is endothermic.

questions.stem_zh: 燃烧蜡烛，最合适的分类是？
questions.stem_en: Burning a candle is best classified as:
questions.explanation_zh: 燃烧向周围释放能量（光和热），是放热反应。
questions.explanation_en: Combustion releases energy (light and heat) to the surroundings, so it is exothermic.

options.en: endothermic, because it has to be lit

questions.stem_zh: 温度从 $21^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 升到 $28^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 的反应，应称为放热还是吸热？
questions.stem_en: A reaction whose mixture rises from $21^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $28^\circ\mathrm{C}$ is exothermic or endothermic?
questions.explanation_zh: 混合物（周围）温度升高，说明能量被释放。
questions.explanation_en: The temperature of the mixture (surroundings) rose, so energy was released.
questions.answer_zh: 放热
questions.answer_en: exothermic

questions.stem_zh: 许多热分解反应需要持续加热才能进行。它们通常是？
questions.stem_en: Many thermal decompositions need a continuous supply of heat. They are usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 需要不断从周围吸收能量，通常是吸热过程。
questions.explanation_en: They take in energy from the surroundings, so they are usually endothermic.

questions.stem_zh: 关于放热与吸热，正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 两者都有能量转移，只是方向不同；可用温度变化作为证据。
questions.explanation_en: Both involve energy transfer, but in opposite directions; temperature change is evidence.

options.zh: 两者都有能量转移，方向相反
options.en: both involve energy transfer, in opposite directions

options.zh: 只有放热才遵守能量观念
吸热过程中周围一定会沸腾
options.en: the surroundings must boil in an endothermic change

questions.stem_zh: 下列金属中，通常最不活泼的是？
questions.stem_en: Which of these metals is usually the least reactive?
questions.explanation_zh: 金的反应性很低；钾、钠、镁都活泼得多。
questions.explanation_en: Gold is very unreactive; potassium, sodium and magnesium are much more reactive.

questions.stem_zh: 把锌放入硫酸铜溶液，通常会观察到？
questions.stem_en: Zinc is placed in copper sulfate solution. You would usually observe:
questions.explanation_zh: 锌比铜活泼，置换出铜，可能看到红棕色固体，蓝色变浅。
questions.explanation_en: Zinc is more reactive than copper, so copper is displaced: brown solid may appear and the blue colour fades.

options.en: copper appears and the blue colour fades

options.zh: 完全没有任何变化，因为锌不活泼
options.en: no change at all, because zinc is unreactive

questions.stem_zh: 铜放入硫酸锌溶液，最可能的结果是？
questions.stem_en: Copper is placed in zinc sulfate solution. The most likely result is:
questions.explanation_zh: 铜不如锌活泼，不能置换锌，通常无明显反应。
questions.explanation_en: Copper is less reactive than zinc, so it cannot displace zinc; there is usually no reaction.

options.en: a large volume of hydrogen is produced

questions.stem_zh: 写出锌与硫酸铜反应的文字方程式。
questions.stem_en: Write the word equation for zinc reacting with copper sulfate.
questions.answer: zinc + copper sulfate -> zinc sulfate + copper
questions.explanation_zh: 更活泼的锌把铜置换出来。
questions.explanation_en: More reactive zinc displaces copper.
accepted: zinc + copper sulfate -> zinc sulfate + copper
zinc + copper sulfate → zinc sulfate + copper
锌 + 硫酸铜 → 硫酸锌 + 铜
questions.answer_zh: 锌 $+$ 硫酸铜 $\rightarrow$ 硫酸锌 $+$ 铜
questions.answer_en: zinc $+$ copper sulfate $\rightarrow$ zinc sulfate $+$ copper

questions.stem_zh: 比较金属与稀酸反应时，一个合理的观察是？
questions.stem_en: A fair observation when comparing metals with dilute acid is:
questions.explanation_zh: 气泡快慢或温度升高等，可比较反应剧烈程度（控制酸的浓度和温度等条件）。
questions.explanation_en: The rate of bubbling or the temperature rise can be compared if conditions such as acid concentration and temperature are controlled.

options.zh: 金属的颜色决定反应性
options.en: the colour of the metal decides reactivity

options.zh: 在相同条件下看冒泡快慢或升温多少
options.en: compare bubbling or temperature rise under the same conditions

options.zh: 只有金会与稀酸迅速反应
options.en: only gold reacts quickly with dilute acid

options.zh: 所有金属与酸的反应完全相同
options.en: every metal reacts in exactly the same way with acid

questions.stem_zh: 铁能否把铜从硫酸铜中置换出来？
questions.stem_en: Can iron displace copper from copper sulfate?
questions.explanation_zh: 铁比铜活泼，可以置换铜。
questions.explanation_en: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it can displace copper.

options.en: yes, because iron is more reactive than copper
no, because iron is the least reactive metal
yes, because copper is more reactive than iron

options.zh: 不能，因为置换只发生在气体中
options.en: no, because displacement only happens in gases

questions.stem_zh: 惰性物质在该反应中的典型行为是？
questions.stem_en: An inert substance in a reaction typically:
questions.explanation_zh: 惰性物质几乎不反应，不会变成目标产物。
questions.explanation_en: It barely reacts and does not turn into the target product.

options.zh: 比所有反应物都更活泼
options.en: is more reactive than every reactant
must increase the mass of product

options.zh: 把方程式中的箭头反过来
options.en: reverses the arrow in the equation

questions.stem_zh: 同样质量的锌，一份纯，一份混有沙子（不反应）。与足量稀酸反应，纯锌产生的氢气？
questions.stem_en: Two equal masses of zinc are used with excess dilute acid. One sample is pure; the other is mixed with unreactive sand. The pure zinc produces:
questions.explanation_zh: 纯样品中可反应的锌更多，产生的氢气更多。
questions.explanation_en: The pure sample contains more zinc that can react, so it produces more hydrogen.

options.zh: 为零，因为纯物质不反应
options.en: none, because pure substances do not react

questions.stem_zh: 收集到的固体产物熔点比数据手册更低、熔程更宽，可能说明？
questions.stem_en: A collected solid product melts lower and over a wider range than the data-book value. This may mean:
questions.explanation_zh: 产物可能不纯，混有杂质或未反应物。
questions.explanation_en: The product may be impure, mixed with impurities or unreacted material.

options.en: the product must be an element

options.zh: 熔点数据永远不能用于产物
options.en: melting points can never be used for products

questions.stem_zh: 为什么样品里的惰性杂质会减少有用产物的质量？
questions.stem_en: Why does an inert impurity in a sample reduce the mass of useful product?
questions.explanation_zh: 惰性成分占用质量，却不参加生成目标产物的反应。
questions.explanation_en: The inert part adds mass but does not take part in making the target product.
accepted: inert impurity does not make product
惰性杂质不生成目标产物
同样质量里真正能反应的物质更少
questions.answer_zh: 同样质量的样品里，能反应的物质变少，惰性杂质又不生成目标产物。
questions.answer_en: There is less reactant that can react in the same mass of sample, and the inert impurity does not make the target product.

questions.stem_zh: 空气中的氮气在许多燃烧反应里可看作？
questions.stem_en: In many combustion reactions, nitrogen in air can be treated as:
questions.explanation_zh: 氮气在这些反应里往往近似惰性，不一定进入燃烧产物。
questions.explanation_en: Nitrogen is often nearly inert in these reactions and does not necessarily enter the combustion product.

options.zh: 比氧气更活泼的反应物
options.en: a more reactive reactant than oxygen

options.zh: 纯净物所以一定参加反应
options.en: a pure substance, so it must react

questions.stem_zh: 若需要纯的晶体产物，实验后通常还要？
questions.stem_en: If you need a pure crystalline product, after the reaction you often have to:
questions.explanation_zh: 通过过滤、结晶等步骤分离和提纯。
questions.explanation_en: Separate and purify, for example by filtering and crystallising.

options.zh: 把文字方程式的箭头反过来写
停止测量熔点，因为已经纯了
options.en: stop checking melting points, because it must already be pure

questions.stem_zh: 对大多数盐来说，温度升高时溶解度通常？
questions.stem_en: For most salts, as temperature rises, solubility usually:
questions.explanation_zh: 大多数盐的溶解度随温度升高而增大。
questions.explanation_en: The solubility of most salts increases as temperature increases.

options.en: suddenly turns into a gas first

questions.stem_zh: 某盐在 $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 溶解度为 $30\ \mathrm{g}/100\ \mathrm{g}$ 水，在 $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 为 $80\ \mathrm{g}/100\ \mathrm{g}$ 水。把 $100\ \mathrm{g}$ 水中的饱和溶液从 $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 冷到 $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$，约析出多少克晶体？
questions.stem_en: A salt dissolves $30\ \mathrm{g}/100\ \mathrm{g}$ water at $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and $80\ \mathrm{g}/100\ \mathrm{g}$ water at $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$. A saturated solution in $100\ \mathrm{g}$ water is cooled from $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$. About how many grams of crystals form?

questions.stem_zh: 饱和溶液的含义是？
questions.stem_en: A saturated solution is one that:
questions.explanation_zh: 在该温度下已溶解了最大量溶质，再加固体会剩下不溶。
questions.explanation_en: It already holds the maximum solute at that temperature; extra solid remains undissolved.

options.zh: 在该温度下不能再溶解更多溶质
options.en: cannot dissolve any more solute at that temperature

questions.stem_zh: 热的盐的饱和溶液缓慢冷却，常用于？
questions.stem_en: Slowly cooling a hot saturated solution of a salt is often used to:
questions.explanation_zh: 冷却结晶可让多余溶质以晶体形式析出，常用于提纯。
questions.explanation_en: Cooling crystallisation lets extra solute come out as crystals, often used to purify a salt.

options.en: turn the salt into an inert gas

options.zh: 使盐结晶析出从而提纯
options.en: crystallise the salt and so purify it

options.zh: 提高所有气体的溶解度
options.en: increase the solubility of every gas

questions.stem_zh: 为什么谈论溶解度时必须说明温度？
questions.stem_en: Why must a solubility value include a temperature?
questions.explanation_zh: 例如同一盐在 $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 和 $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$ 的溶解度通常不同。
questions.explanation_en: The same salt usually has different solubilities at $20^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and at $70^\circ\mathrm{C}$.
accepted: 必须标明温度因为溶解度随温度改变
questions.answer_zh: 溶解度随温度变化，不标明温度就不完整。
questions.answer_en: Solubility changes with temperature, so the value is incomplete without it.

questions.stem_zh: 溶解度曲线上，横轴通常表示？
questions.stem_en: On a typical solubility curve, the horizontal axis usually shows:
questions.explanation_zh: 横轴是温度，纵轴是溶解度。
questions.explanation_en: Temperature is usually horizontal; solubility is vertical.

questions.stem_zh: 下列哪一项是不可再生资源？
questions.stem_en: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
questions.explanation_zh: 石油形成极慢，属于不可再生；风、太阳能和可持续木材是可再生的。
questions.explanation_en: Oil forms far too slowly to be replaced, so it is non-renewable; wind, solar and sustainable timber are renewable.

questions.stem_zh: 可再生资源的核心含义是？
questions.stem_en: The core idea of a renewable resource is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 能在人类使用的时间尺度上得到补充。
questions.explanation_en: Can be replaced on a human timescale of use.

options.zh: 能在人类使用的时间尺度上补充
options.en: can be replaced on a human timescale

options.zh: 使用时一定完全没有环境影响
options.en: has zero environmental impact when used

questions.stem_zh: 回收铝罐主要的意义是？
questions.stem_en: A main reason to recycle aluminium cans is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 减少对新矿的需求和通常所需的大量提炼能量。矿本身仍是不可再生的。
questions.explanation_en: Reduce demand for new ore and the large amount of energy usually needed to extract it. The ore itself is still non-renewable.

options.zh: 让铝土矿立刻变成可再生资源
options.en: turn bauxite into a renewable resource immediately

options.zh: 减少开采新矿并节省提炼能量
options.en: reduce new mining and save extraction energy

questions.stem_zh: 各举一个可再生资源和一个不可再生资源的例子。
questions.stem_en: Give one example of a renewable resource and one example of a non-renewable resource.
questions.explanation_zh: 只要一对分类正确即可，例如风与石油、可持续木材与天然气。
questions.explanation_en: Any correctly classified pair is fine, such as wind and oil, or sustainable timber and natural gas.
questions.answer_zh: 例如：太阳能（可再生）和煤（不可再生）。
questions.answer_en: For example: solar energy (renewable) and coal (non-renewable).

questions.stem_zh: 若森林砍伐快于再生长，这样使用木材应当看作？
questions.stem_en: If a forest is cut down faster than it can regrow, that use of timber should be seen as:
questions.explanation_zh: 补充跟不上消耗，这种使用就不再可持续，不能简单称为可再生利用。
questions.explanation_en: Replacement cannot keep up, so the use is not sustainable and should not simply be called renewable use.

options.zh: 一定仍然完全可再生且无影响

options.en: turning timber into a metal ore

questions.stem_zh: 煤、石油、天然气被归为不可再生，主要是因为？
questions.stem_en: Coal, oil and natural gas are classed as non-renewable mainly because:
questions.explanation_zh: 它们的自然形成远慢于人类消耗的速度。
questions.explanation_en: They form naturally far more slowly than humans use them.

options.zh: 自然形成远慢于被消耗的速度
options.en: they form far more slowly than they are used

questions.stem_zh: “明天下午有雷阵雨”描述的是？
questions.stem_en: “There will be a thunderstorm tomorrow afternoon” describes:
questions.explanation_zh: 针对具体时间的短期状况，是天气。
questions.explanation_en: It is a short-term condition for a specific time, so it is weather.

questions.stem_zh: “该地区多年平均年降雨量很高，全年温暖”描述的是？
questions.stem_en: “This region has a high average annual rainfall and is warm all year” describes:
questions.explanation_zh: 这是长期平均状况，属于气候。
questions.explanation_en: This is a long-term average pattern, so it is climate.

questions.stem_zh: 为什么不能只用连续三天偏凉来否定长期变暖趋势？
questions.stem_en: Why can three cooler days not, by themselves, disprove a long-term warming trend?
questions.explanation_zh: 三天是天气的短期波动；气候趋势需要长期数据。
questions.explanation_en: Three days are short-term weather; a climate trend needs a long record.

options.zh: 因为气候必须每天完全相同
options.en: because climate means every day is identical

options.zh: 因为那只是短期天气，气候看长期记录
options.en: because that is short-term weather, and climate uses a long record

options.zh: 因为温度计只能测气候，不能测天气
options.en: because thermometers can measure climate but not weather

questions.stem_zh: 用一句话区分天气和气候。
questions.stem_en: In one sentence, distinguish weather and climate.
questions.answer: weather is short term, climate is long term
questions.explanation_zh: 关键差别是时间尺度：日、周相对年、十年。
questions.explanation_en: The key difference is timescale: days or weeks versus years or decades.
accepted: weather is short term, climate is long term
天气是短期的，气候是长期的平均状况
天气看短时间，气候看长期型态
questions.answer_zh: 天气是短期的大气状况，气候是长期的平均天气型态。
questions.answer_en: Weather is the short-term state of the atmosphere; climate is the long-term pattern of weather.

questions.stem_zh: 新加坡某一天比平常稍凉，这最适合称为？
questions.stem_en: A day in Singapore that is a little cooler than usual is best described as:
questions.explanation_zh: 这是短期变化，属于天气；气候仍然是热带温暖潮湿。
questions.explanation_en: It is a short-term variation, so it is weather; the climate is still tropical, warm and humid.

options.zh: 天气和气候是同一个词
options.en: weather and climate mean the same

options.zh: 长期气候记录被这一天完全改写
options.en: this one day rewrites the long-term climate record

options.zh: 一次天气变化，不等于气候已经改变
options.en: a weather variation, not by itself a change of climate

questions.stem_zh: 描述气候时，下列哪一种说法最合适？
questions.stem_en: Which is the most suitable way to describe climate?
questions.explanation_zh: 用长期平均和通常范围，而不是只引用某一天。
questions.explanation_en: Use long-term averages and the usual range, not a single day alone.

options.zh: 用多年的平均状况和通常范围
options.en: use averages and the usual range over many years
use cloud cover from one day only

questions.stem_zh: 关于地球气候，较准确的说法是？
questions.stem_en: A fair statement about Earth’s climate is that:
questions.explanation_zh: 气候并非永恒不变，历史上有过冰期和较暖期等长期变化。
questions.explanation_en: Climate is not fixed for ever; there have been long-term changes such as ice ages and warmer periods.

options.zh: 气候从未发生过任何变化
options.en: climate has never changed at all

options.zh: 气候会在很长的时间尺度上变化，存在长期循环
options.en: climate can change over long timescales and there are long-term cycles

options.zh: 气候每小时精确重复一次循环
options.en: climate repeats an exact cycle every hour

options.zh: 只有天气存在，气候不存在
options.en: only weather exists; climate does not

questions.stem_zh: 大规模火山喷发可能在一段时间里使地表变凉，是因为？
questions.stem_en: A large volcanic eruption may cool the surface for a time because:
questions.explanation_zh: 喷发把尘埃和气体送进大气，可能挡住部分阳光。
questions.explanation_en: It can inject dust and gases into the atmosphere, which may block some sunlight.

options.zh: 尘埃和气体进入大气，可能挡住部分阳光
options.en: dust and gases enter the atmosphere and may block some sunlight

options.zh: 火山会立刻停止地球公转
options.en: volcanoes instantly stop Earth orbiting the Sun

options.zh: 火山把所有海洋变成纯净物
options.en: volcanoes turn all oceans into pure substances

options.zh: 火山只改变明天一小时的天气预报，不影响大气
options.en: volcanoes change only one hour of tomorrow’s forecast and not the atmosphere

questions.stem_zh: 大气中某些气体浓度改变，可能影响气候，是因为它们可以？
questions.stem_en: A change in the concentration of some atmospheric gases may affect climate because those gases can:
questions.explanation_zh: 某些气体（如二氧化碳）会影响地球保留的能量。
questions.explanation_en: Some gases (such as carbon dioxide) affect how much energy Earth keeps.

options.zh: 把所有盐的溶解度变为零
options.en: make the solubility of every salt zero

options.zh: 影响地球保留多少能量
options.en: affect how much energy Earth keeps

questions.stem_zh: 举出一个可导致气候长期变化的自然因素。
questions.stem_en: Give one natural factor that can contribute to long-term climate change.
questions.explanation_zh: 自然因素不止一种，答对其中一类即可。
questions.explanation_en: There is more than one natural factor; any appropriate one is fine.
questions.answer_zh: 例如火山喷发，或地球轨道与轴向的缓慢变化。
questions.answer_en: For example volcanic eruptions, or slow changes in Earth’s orbit and tilt.

questions.stem_zh: “以前也有自然的气候循环，所以今天人类活动不可能有影响。”这个推论的问题是？
questions.stem_en: “Natural climate cycles existed in the past, so human activity cannot have an effect today.” The problem with this claim is:
questions.explanation_zh: 自然循环与人类对大气的额外影响可以同时存在，前者并不能自动排除后者。
questions.explanation_en: Natural cycles and extra human effects on the atmosphere can exist together; the first does not automatically rule out the second.

options.zh: 气候循环每小时发生一次，所以说法成立
options.en: climate cycles happen every hour, so the claim is true

options.zh: 人类活动从来不会改变大气
options.en: human activity never changes the atmosphere

options.zh: 天气和气候是同一个词
options.en: weather and climate are the same word

questions.explanation_en: Clotting.

questions.stem_zh: 栖息地指？
questions.stem_en: A habitat is:
questions.explanation_en: The place where an organism lives.

options.en: the place where an organism lives

questions.stem_zh: 减少入侵风险，更应？
questions.stem_en: To reduce invasion risk, it is better to:
questions.explanation_en: Prevent arrival and not release pets.

options.zh: 预防进入新地区，不随意放生
options.en: prevent entry to new areas and not release pets

questions.stem_zh: 肌肉对骨头的作用，最准确的是？
questions.stem_en: The most accurate description of how a muscle acts on a bone is that it:
questions.explanation_zh: 肌肉只能收缩，从而拉骨头。
questions.explanation_en: A muscle can only contract, and so pull a bone.

options.en: can only push the bone away
can only contract and so pull the bone

options.zh: 既能随意推也能随意变成韧带
options.en: can push at will and can also turn into a ligament
is not attached to the skeleton

questions.stem_zh: 屈肘时，通常发生的是？
questions.stem_en: When the elbow bends, what usually happens?
questions.explanation_zh: 肱二头肌收缩，肱三头肌舒张。
questions.explanation_en: The biceps contracts and the triceps relaxes.

options.zh: 肱二头肌收缩，肱三头肌舒张
两块肌肉同时尽量收缩并互相推开骨头
options.en: both muscles contract as hard as possible and push the bone

options.zh: 肱三头肌收缩，肱二头肌也必须同时同样收缩
options.en: the triceps contracts and the biceps must contract equally at the same time

questions.stem_zh: 拮抗肌成对工作，是因为？
questions.stem_en: Antagonistic muscles work in pairs because:
questions.explanation_zh: 一块肌肉只能把骨头拉向一个方向，反向要靠另一块。
questions.explanation_en: One muscle can only pull a bone one way; the opposite movement needs the other muscle.

options.zh: 一块肌肉可以完成所有方向的推和拉
options.en: one muscle can push and pull in every direction

options.zh: 一块肌肉只能拉向一个方向，反向要靠另一块
options.en: one muscle can only pull one way, so the opposite movement needs the other

options.zh: 血液会代替肌肉拉动骨骼
options.en: blood pulls the bones instead of muscles

questions.stem_zh: 肌腱和韧带的作用有何不同？
questions.stem_en: How do the roles of a tendon and a ligament differ?
questions.answer: tendon muscle to bone, ligament bone to bone
questions.explanation_en: Do not swap the two.
accepted: tendon muscle to bone, ligament bone to bone
tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone
肌腱连接肌肉和骨，韧带连接骨和骨
肌腱连肌肉与骨，韧带连骨与骨
questions.answer_zh: 肌腱把肌肉连到骨上；韧带连接骨与骨。
questions.answer_en: Tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone.

questions.stem_zh: 伸直肘关节时，主要收缩的是？
questions.stem_en: To straighten the elbow, the muscle that mainly contracts is the:
questions.explanation_zh: 肱三头肌收缩，把前臂拉直。
questions.explanation_en: The triceps contracts and pulls the forearm straight.

questions.stem_zh: 关节的作用是？
questions.stem_en: The role of a joint is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 关节是骨与骨相连并允许运动的部位。
questions.explanation_en: A joint is where bones meet and movement is allowed.

options.en: allow the connected bones to move
make red blood cells in every joint

options.zh: 进行有氧呼吸的全部过程
options.en: carry out all of aerobic respiration

questions.stem_zh: 主要负责运输氧气的是？
questions.stem_en: Oxygen is transported mainly by:
questions.explanation_zh: 红细胞含血红蛋白，主要运输氧气。
questions.explanation_en: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin and mainly transport oxygen.

questions.stem_zh: 血小板的主要功能是？
questions.stem_en: The main function of platelets is:
questions.explanation_zh: 血小板参与凝血、帮助止血。
questions.explanation_en: Platelets are involved in clotting, which helps stop bleeding.

options.zh: 进行有氧呼吸的全部步骤
options.en: carrying out every step of aerobic respiration

questions.stem_zh: 白细胞的主要功能是？
questions.stem_en: The main function of white blood cells is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 白细胞帮助抵御病原体。
questions.explanation_en: White blood cells help defend against pathogens.

options.zh: 形成血浆蛋白以外的全部骨骼
options.en: form the entire skeleton besides plasma proteins

questions.stem_zh: 血浆运输哪些物质？举出至少两项。
questions.stem_en: Name at least two things transported by plasma.
questions.explanation_zh: 血浆是液体部分，运输许多溶解的物质和热。
questions.explanation_en: Plasma is the liquid part and carries many dissolved substances and heat.
questions.answer_zh: 例如养分、激素、二氧化碳、废物或热。
questions.answer_en: For example nutrients, hormones, carbon dioxide, wastes or heat.

questions.stem_zh: 血液的液体部分称为？
questions.stem_en: The liquid part of blood is called:
questions.explanation_en: The liquid part is plasma.

questions.stem_zh: 下列配对正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which pairing is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 红细胞—运氧；白细胞—防御；血小板—凝血；血浆—运输溶解物质。
questions.explanation_en: Red cells—oxygen; white cells—defence; platelets—clotting; plasma—dissolved substances.

options.zh: 红细胞运输氧气，血小板参与凝血
options.en: red cells transport oxygen; platelets help in clotting

options.zh: 血小板是主要运氧细胞，红细胞只负责凝血
options.en: platelets are the main oxygen carriers; red cells only clot

options.zh: 血浆不能运输任何物质
白细胞只存在于植物体内
options.en: white cells exist only in plants

questions.stem_zh: 气体交换的主要场所是？
questions.stem_en: The main site of gas exchange is the:
questions.explanation_zh: 气体交换主要发生在肺泡与血液之间。
questions.explanation_en: Gas exchange happens mainly between the alveoli and the blood.

questions.stem_zh: 在肺泡处，通常发生的气体方向是？
questions.stem_en: At the alveoli, the usual direction of the gases is:
questions.explanation_zh: 氧气进入血液，二氧化碳离开血液进入肺泡。
questions.explanation_en: Oxygen enters the blood; carbon dioxide leaves the blood and enters the alveoli.

options.zh: 氧气进入血液，二氧化碳离开血液
options.en: oxygen enters the blood; carbon dioxide leaves the blood
both gases only enter and never leave

options.zh: 二氧化碳进入血液，氧气全部留在气管
options.en: carbon dioxide enters the blood and all oxygen stays in the trachea

options.zh: 气体交换只在关节处发生
options.en: gas exchange happens only at joints

questions.stem_zh: 胸廓和膈肌的运动主要是为了？
questions.stem_en: Movements of the ribcage and diaphragm are mainly for:
questions.explanation_zh: 这是通气，使空气进出肺。
questions.explanation_en: This is ventilation, moving air in and out of the lungs.

options.zh: 在肺泡腔内完成全部有氧呼吸
options.en: completing all of aerobic respiration in the alveolar cavity
moving air in and out of the lungs (ventilation)

questions.stem_zh: 通气（呼吸运动）和细胞里的呼吸作用有什么不同？
questions.stem_en: How does ventilation differ from respiration in cells?
questions.answer: ventilation moves air; respiration releases energy in cells
questions.explanation_zh: 两个词在日常口语里常混用，课上要分开。
questions.explanation_en: Everyday speech often mixes the words; in class they must be kept apart.
accepted: ventilation moves air; respiration releases energy in cells
ventilation is air in and out of lungs; respiration is in cells
通气是空气进出肺，呼吸作用在细胞中释放能量
呼吸运动是通气，呼吸作用在细胞内
questions.answer_zh: 通气是空气进出肺；呼吸作用在细胞中释放能量。
questions.answer_en: Ventilation moves air in and out of the lungs; respiration releases energy in cells.

questions.stem_zh: 气管中的软骨有助于？
questions.stem_en: Cartilage in the trachea helps to:
questions.explanation_zh: 软骨支撑气管，保持气道开放。
questions.explanation_en: Cartilage supports the trachea and helps keep the airway open.

options.en: transport oxygen in place of red cells

options.zh: 把血液变成血浆以外的固体骨
options.en: turn blood into bone other than plasma

questions.stem_zh: 下列顺序正确的是？
questions.stem_en: Which order is correct?
questions.explanation_zh: 空气经气管、支气管到达肺泡。
questions.explanation_en: Air travels via the trachea and bronchi to the alveoli.

options.zh: 气管 → 支气管 → 肺泡
肺泡 → 胃 → 气管作为吸气路径
options.en: alveoli → stomach → trachea as the path for inhaled air

options.zh: 关节 → 韧带 → 肺泡
血浆 → 气管 → 体外作为吸气顺序
options.en: plasma → trachea → outside as the inhalation sequence

questions.stem_zh: 扩散是指粒子的净移动方向为？
questions.stem_en: In diffusion, the net movement of particles is from:
questions.explanation_en: From higher concentration to lower concentration.

questions.stem_zh: 肺泡中氧气进入血液，是因为？
questions.stem_en: Oxygen enters the blood at the alveoli because:
questions.explanation_zh: 肺泡气中氧气浓度高于血液，氧气向低浓度处扩散。
questions.explanation_en: The oxygen concentration is higher in alveolar air than in the blood, so oxygen diffuses into the blood.

options.en: the concentration is higher in the blood

options.zh: 氧气主动从低浓度被推到更高浓度
options.en: oxygen is pushed from low to even higher concentration

options.zh: 肺泡气中氧气浓度高于血液
options.en: the concentration is higher in the alveolar air than in the blood

options.zh: 血小板把氧气泵进骨头

questions.stem_zh: 下列哪一项是肺泡适合气体交换的特征？
questions.stem_en: Which is an adaptation of alveoli for gas exchange?
questions.explanation_zh: 壁薄、表面积大、湿润并有丰富毛细血管。
questions.explanation_en: Thin walls, a large surface area, a moist surface and a rich capillary supply.

options.en: very thick walls, to slow diffusion
thin walls and a large total surface area

options.zh: 表面保持完全干燥且只有一个大气囊
options.en: a completely dry surface and only one large air sac

questions.stem_zh: 为什么通气有助于肺泡处的气体扩散？
questions.stem_en: Why does ventilation help diffusion at the alveoli?
questions.explanation_zh: 没有浓度差，净扩散就会减慢。
questions.explanation_en: Without a gradient, net diffusion slows.
accepted: it refreshes the air so oxygen stays high and CO2 stays low
更新空气，保持氧气高、二氧化碳低
不断更新肺泡空气以保持浓度差
questions.answer_zh: 通气更新肺泡空气，维持氧气高、二氧化碳低的浓度差。
questions.answer_en: Ventilation refreshes alveolar air, keeping oxygen high and carbon dioxide low, so the gradient is maintained.

questions.stem_zh: 血液中的二氧化碳进入肺泡，是因为？
questions.stem_en: Carbon dioxide enters the alveoli from the blood because:
questions.explanation_zh: 血液中二氧化碳浓度更高，向肺泡扩散。
questions.explanation_en: The concentration is higher in the blood, so it diffuses into the alveoli.

options.zh: 肺泡中二氧化碳浓度更高
options.en: the concentration is higher in the alveoli

options.zh: 韧带把二氧化碳拉过去
options.en: ligaments pull the carbon dioxide across

options.zh: 血液中二氧化碳浓度高于肺泡
options.en: the concentration is higher in the blood than in the alveoli

questions.stem_zh: 丰富的毛细血管有助于气体交换，是因为？
questions.stem_en: A rich capillary supply helps gas exchange because:
questions.explanation_zh: 血液能迅速运走氧气、送来二氧化碳，有助于维持浓度差。
questions.explanation_en: Blood can carry oxygen away and bring carbon dioxide, helping to maintain the gradient.

options.zh: 气体可以被迅速运走或送来，维持浓度差
options.en: gases can be carried away or delivered quickly, maintaining the gradient

options.zh: 毛细血管会把肺泡变成关节

options.en: the alveolar walls then become thicker

questions.stem_zh: 蛋白质的主要作用是？
questions.stem_en: The main role of protein is:
questions.explanation_zh: 蛋白质主要用于生长和修复。
questions.explanation_en: Protein is used mainly for growth and repair.

options.zh: 进行气体在肺泡外的扩散即可，无需饮食
options.en: allowing diffusion outside alveoli so that diet is unnecessary

questions.stem_zh: 均衡饮食的含义最接近？
questions.stem_en: A balanced diet is closest to:
questions.explanation_zh: 适量提供各类营养素、水和纤维。
questions.explanation_en: Providing suitable amounts of each type of nutrient, plus water and fibre.

options.zh: 适量摄入各类营养素、水和纤维
options.en: suitable amounts of each nutrient, plus water and fibre

options.zh: 只吃一种食物，越多越好
options.en: eating as much as possible of one food only

options.zh: 完全不摄入脂肪和糖类
options.en: cutting out all fat and carbohydrate

questions.stem_zh: 糖类和脂肪在饮食中的主要共同作用是？
questions.stem_en: A main shared role of carbohydrate and fat in the diet is to:
questions.explanation_zh: 两者都是重要的能量来源。
questions.explanation_en: Both are important sources of energy.

questions.stem_zh: 纤维在饮食中的一种作用是什么？
questions.stem_en: Give one role of fibre in the diet.
questions.answer: helps food move through the gut
questions.explanation_zh: 纤维不是主要的供能营养素，但对肠道功能重要。
questions.explanation_en: Fibre is not a main energy nutrient, but it matters for the gut.
accepted: helps food move through the gut
questions.answer_zh: 帮助食物和粪便在肠道中移动。
questions.answer_en: It helps food and faeces move through the gut.

questions.stem_zh: 维生素和矿物质的特点是？
questions.stem_en: Vitamins and minerals are typically:
questions.explanation_zh: 需要量较小，但缺乏可能导致缺乏症。
questions.explanation_en: Needed in smaller amounts, but a lack can cause deficiency disease.

options.zh: 只存在于金属矿中，不能出现在食物里
options.en: found only in metal ores, never in food

options.zh: 需要量较小，缺乏时仍可能引起疾病
options.en: needed in smaller amounts, but a lack can still cause disease

questions.stem_zh: 只吃大量某一种“健康食物”、完全缺少蛋白质，算均衡吗？
questions.stem_en: Is it balanced to eat large amounts of one “healthy” food and no protein?
questions.explanation_zh: 种类不全就不均衡，长期缺蛋白质会影响生长和修复。
questions.explanation_en: Missing a whole group means it is not balanced; lack of protein affects growth and repair.

options.zh: 不算，因为种类不全、蛋白质不足
options.en: no, because a group is missing and protein is lacking
yes, because the amount eaten is large

options.zh: 算，因为健康食物可以代替所有营养素
options.en: yes, because one healthy food can replace every nutrient

options.zh: 不算，因为均衡饮食禁止所有水果
options.en: no, because a balanced diet bans all fruit

questions.stem_zh: 同样质量下，通常提供能量最多的是？
questions.stem_en: For the same mass, which usually provides the most energy?
questions.explanation_zh: 脂肪单位质量的能量通常高于糖类或蛋白质。
questions.explanation_en: Fat usually provides more energy per unit mass than carbohydrate or protein.

options.zh: 纤维本身作为最主要供能物质
options.en: fibre as the main energy source

questions.stem_zh: 食物对人体的一个关键作用是提供？
questions.stem_en: A key role of food for the body is to provide:
questions.explanation_zh: 食物储存化学能，可供生命活动使用。
questions.explanation_en: Food stores chemical energy that can be used for life processes.

options.zh: 只提供无法使用的惰性沙子
options.en: only inert sand that cannot be used

options.zh: 肺泡壁增厚所需的软骨
options.en: cartilage needed to thicken alveolar walls

options.zh: 替代所有氧气使呼吸不再需要
options.en: a substitute for all oxygen so respiration is unnecessary

questions.stem_zh: 长期摄入能量远高于消耗，可能发生？
questions.stem_en: If energy intake stays much higher than energy use, a likely result is:
questions.explanation_zh: 多余能量可能以脂肪形式储存。
questions.explanation_en: Extra energy may be stored as fat.

options.zh: 体内能量储存自动变为零
options.en: body energy stores automatically fall to zero

options.zh: 蛋白质不再具有任何功能
多余能量可能以脂肪形式储存
options.en: extra energy may be stored as fat

options.zh: 扩散会反向从低到高且永久停止通气
options.en: diffusion permanently reverses from low to high and ventilation stops

questions.stem_zh: 课堂用燃烧食物加热水来比较能量时，为什么结果往往偏低？
questions.stem_en: In a class experiment that burns food to heat water, why is the energy value often too low?
questions.answer: heat is lost to the surroundings
questions.explanation_zh: 这是粗略比较，不是精密测量。
questions.explanation_en: It is a rough comparison, not a precise measurement.
accepted: heat is lost to the surroundings
not all heat goes into the water
不是所有热都进入水中
questions.answer_zh: 部分热量会散失到周围空气中，没有全部用于升高水温。
questions.answer_en: Some heat is lost to the surrounding air and does not all go into raising the water temperature.

questions.stem_zh: 活动量很大的人，通常需要？
questions.stem_en: A very active person usually needs:
questions.explanation_zh: 活动耗能更多，通常需要更多能量摄入（仍要保持均衡）。
questions.explanation_en: Activity uses more energy, so intake usually needs to be higher (while still remaining balanced).

options.zh: 只需要纤维，不需要任何其他营养
options.en: fibre only, and no other nutrients

options.zh: 比活动少时更多的能量（并仍要均衡）
options.en: more energy than when less active, while still eating a balanced diet

questions.stem_zh: 比较两种食物时，只看能量高低是否足够判断哪一种更适合？
questions.stem_en: When comparing two foods, is energy content alone enough to decide which is more suitable?
questions.explanation_zh: 还要考虑其他营养素、份量和需要。
questions.explanation_en: Other nutrients, portion size and need also matter.

options.zh: 不够，还要看其他营养素、份量和需要
options.en: no: other nutrients, portion size and need also matter

options.zh: 足够，能量最高的一定最好
options.en: yes: the highest-energy food is always best

options.zh: 足够，能量最低的一定最好
options.en: yes: the lowest-energy food is always best

options.zh: 食物不含能量，所以不必比较
options.en: food contains no energy, so comparison is unnecessary

questions.stem_zh: 一氧化碳对血液运输氧气的影响是？
questions.stem_en: Carbon monoxide affects oxygen transport by:
questions.explanation_zh: 它与血红蛋白结合，减少可运输的氧气。
questions.explanation_en: It binds to haemoglobin and reduces the oxygen that can be carried.

options.zh: 增加血浆中的氧气至无限
options.en: raising oxygen in plasma without limit

options.zh: 与血红蛋白结合，减少氧气运输
options.en: binding to haemoglobin and reducing oxygen transport

options.zh: 只损害韧带，不影响血液
options.en: damaging ligaments only, not the blood

questions.stem_zh: 焦油损害肺泡，主要影响？
questions.stem_en: Tar damaging the alveoli mainly affects:
questions.explanation_zh: 有效气体交换面积减小，交换变难。
questions.explanation_en: The effective surface for gas exchange is reduced, so exchange is harder.

options.en: tendons attaching instead to the trachea

options.zh: 使扩散必须从低浓度到高浓度
options.en: forcing diffusion to run from low to high concentration

questions.stem_zh: 长期能量摄入远高于消耗，主要相关风险是？
questions.stem_en: A long-term energy intake well above use is mainly linked with:
questions.explanation_zh: 与超重及一些心脏和代谢问题的风险上升有关。
questions.explanation_en: It is linked with overweight and a higher risk of some heart and metabolic problems.

options.zh: 肺泡数目瞬间增加十倍且无任何风险
options.en: an instant ten-fold increase in alveoli and no risk

options.zh: 蛋白质功能完全消失于一天之内
options.en: protein function vanishing completely in a single day

options.zh: 超重及相关健康风险上升
options.en: overweight and a higher related health risk

questions.stem_zh: 写出吸烟中一种有害物质及其一种危害。
questions.stem_en: Name one harmful substance in cigarette smoke and one effect it has.
questions.explanation_zh: 能把物质和结构/功能联系起来即可。
questions.explanation_en: Link the substance to a structure or function.
accepted: 一氧化碳减少氧气运输
questions.answer_zh: 例如一氧化碳减少氧气运输，或焦油损害肺泡。
questions.answer_en: For example, carbon monoxide reduces oxygen transport, or tar damages alveoli.

questions.stem_zh: 尼古丁对循环系统的一种影响是？
questions.stem_en: One effect of nicotine on the circulation is that it can:
questions.explanation_zh: 尼古丁可使血管收缩，加重心脏负担。
questions.explanation_en: Nicotine can narrow blood vessels and add strain to the heart.

options.zh: 把血液全部变成纯氧气
options.en: turn all of the blood into pure oxygen

options.zh: 使血红蛋白只能运输纤维

options.en: be completely harmless to the heart

options.zh: 使血管收缩，心脏工作更费力
options.en: narrow blood vessels so the heart has to work harder

questions.stem_zh: 关于饮食与健康，较准确的说法是？
questions.stem_en: A fair statement about diet and health is:
questions.explanation_zh: 长期习惯更重要，不能把一餐绝对化，但风险可以累积。

questions.stem_en: A market exists when:
questions.explanation_en: Buyers and sellers can trade.

options.zh: 买方和卖方能够就一种物品或服务进行交易
options.en: buyers and sellers can trade a good or a service

options.zh: 必须拥有一座有招牌的大楼
options.en: there must be a building with a shop sign
only the government can buy and sell
the price must always be zero

questions.stem_zh: 某种物品的价格上升，通常传递的信息是？
questions.stem_en: A rise in the price of a good usually transmits the information that:
questions.explanation_en: It is more scarce, or demand is stronger.

options.en: it has become a free good
it is more scarce, or demand is stronger
factors of production are no longer needed

questions.stem_zh: 价格较高时，对生产者的一种典型激励是？
questions.stem_en: When the price is higher, a typical incentive for producers is to:
questions.explanation_en: Increase supply.

options.zh: 把该物品变成自由物品
options.en: turn the good into a free good

questions.stem_zh: 价格机制如何配置资源？
questions.stem_en: How does the price mechanism allocate resources?
questions.answer: 把资源吸引到价格更高、更被需要的用途
questions.explanation_zh: 价格同时提供信息与激励。
questions.explanation_en: Price provides both information and incentives.
accepted: 把资源吸引到价格更高、更被需要的用途
通过价格升降引导资源
it draws resources toward higher-priced, more needed uses
questions.answer_zh: 通过价格升降，把资源吸引到更被需要、价格更高的用途。
questions.answer_en: Through rises and falls in price, it draws resources toward more needed, higher-priced uses.

questions.stem_zh: 校内二手书群里的成交，算不算市场？
questions.stem_en: Do trades in a school second-hand book group count as a market?
questions.explanation_zh: 算，因为买卖双方在交易。
questions.explanation_en: Yes, because buyers and sellers are trading.

options.en: no, because there is no building

options.zh: 不算，因为学生不能参与市场
options.en: no, because students cannot take part in a market

options.zh: 只有纸质布告栏才算市场
options.en: only a paper notice board counts as a market

options.zh: 算，只要买方和卖方能够交易
options.en: yes, so long as buyers and sellers can trade

questions.stem_zh: 价格下降时，消费者往往会被激励去？
questions.stem_en: When the price falls, consumers are often encouraged to:
questions.explanation_en: Buy more.

options.zh: 把供给曲线改称为欲望
options.en: rename the supply curve as wants

questions.stem_en: Name two roles of the price mechanism.
questions.explanation_zh: 升降的价格同时做这两件事。
questions.explanation_en: Rising and falling prices do both.
questions.answer_zh: 传递信息，并提供激励（从而配置资源）。
questions.answer_en: Transmitting information and providing incentives (and so allocating resources).

questions.stem_en: Does the price mechanism work perfectly in every case?
questions.explanation_en: Not necessarily; markets can fail.

options.zh: 是，而且不存在市场失灵
options.en: yes, and market failure cannot occur

options.en: not necessarily; later we will see that markets can also fail

options.zh: 市场必须是一座大楼才可能失灵
options.en: a market can fail only if it is a building

questions.stem_zh: 有效需求要求消费者？
questions.stem_en: Effective demand requires that consumers are:
questions.explanation_en: Willing and able to buy.

options.zh: 只需要“想要”，不必能够支付
options.en: only required to “want” it, without being able to pay

options.zh: 只能在价格为零时购买
options.en: able to buy only when the price is zero

questions.stem_en: Other things equal, when the price rises, quantity demanded usually:

options.en: falls (a movement along the demand curve)

questions.stem_en: The intersection E of D and S in the diagram shows:
questions.explanation_en: Equilibrium price and quantity.

options.zh: 均衡价格 Pe 与均衡数量 Qe
options.en: equilibrium price Pe and equilibrium quantity Qe

options.zh: 生产可能性曲线上的 C 点
options.en: point C on a production possibility curve

questions.stem_zh: 价格高于均衡时，通常会出现？

过剩（供给量大于需求量）
options.en: a surplus (quantity supplied greater than quantity demanded)

questions.stem_zh: 什么是供给？
questions.stem_en: What is supply?

accepted: 生产者愿意并且能够出售的数量
the quantity producers are willing and able to sell
questions.answer_zh: 在一定时期内、各种可能价格下，生产者愿意并且能够出售的数量。
questions.answer_en: The quantity producers are willing and able to sell, at each possible price, over a period of time.

questions.explanation_en: The price comes under upward pressure.
accepted: quantity demanded greater than quantity supplied
questions.answer_zh: 短缺（需求量大于供给量）。
questions.answer_en: A shortage (quantity demanded greater than quantity supplied).

options.en: only a movement along a given demand curve, with demand itself unchanged

options.en: equilibrium ceasing to exist in any market

questions.stem_zh: 本课对弹性与多因素移动的深度是？

questions.explanation_en: The types of movement are separated first; finer calculations are left for a later lesson and for IGCSE.

options.zh: 必须立刻完成全部 IGCSE 交叉弹性计算
options.en: every IGCSE cross-elasticity calculation must be finished at once

options.zh: 八年级先分清沿曲线移动与曲线移动，更细的内容留到后课和 IGCSE
options.en: Year 8 first separates movements along a curve from shifts of a curve; finer work is left for a later lesson and for IGCSE
demand and supply need not be defined

options.zh: 图中的 E 点没有意义
options.en: point E in the diagram has no meaning

questions.explanation_en: How strongly quantity demanded responds to a change in price.

options.zh: 需求量对价格变动的反应程度
options.en: how strongly quantity demanded responds to a change in price

options.zh: 一种物品是不是自由物品
options.en: whether a good is a free good
the official name of an exchange rate

options.zh: 生产要素的数量是否永远固定
options.en: whether the quantity of factors is fixed for ever

questions.explanation_en: Elastic.

accepted: 生产者更有时间调整产量
有时间增加或减少生产
producers have more time to adjust output
there is more time to change production
questions.answer_zh: 生产者更有时间调整产量。
questions.answer_en: Producers have more time to adjust output.

options.en: fall sharply, because demand is more elastic

questions.explanation_en: Not necessarily fall, which is enough to understand at this introductory level.

questions.explanation_en: The idea is established first; exact formulae are left for IGCSE.

options.en: every income- and cross-elasticity calculation must be mastered

options.zh: 弹性在八年级完全不讨论
options.en: elasticity is not discussed at all in Year 8
every good has the same elasticity

questions.explanation_zh: 自由市场未能有效配置资源。

options.zh: 自由市场未能达到社会希望的有效配置
options.en: a free market has not reached the efficient allocation society would want

options.zh: 任何自己不喜欢的价格
options.en: any price one happens to dislike
factors of production no longer exist

the light is not used up by one more ship

questions.stem_zh: 本课对政策评价的深度是？

options.zh: 市场失灵在八年级完全不讨论

questions.answer_zh: 例如：交换媒介和价值尺度。
questions.answer_en: For example: a medium of exchange and a unit of account.

questions.stem_zh: 商业银行的一项入门作用是？

options.zh: 制定全部商品的最高价格
options.en: set a maximum price for every good

options.zh: 取代所有企业进行生产
吸收存款，提供支付便利，并向合格借款人提供信贷

questions.stem_zh: 向银行借款之后，通常应当？
